第二部
实验
en:
II
THE EXPERIMENT

children: 布尔什维克革命的道德本性，继承自它诞生于其中的那场战争。
The moral nature of the Bolshevik Revolution was inherited from the war in which it was born.

战争已经足够清楚、而且是以一种非常实际的方式再次确认……现代资本主义社会，尤其是先进国家，已经完全成熟到可以过渡到社会主义。例如，如果德国能够从一个中央机构组织起六千六百万人的经济生活……那么，只要无产者群众的斗争由有阶级觉悟的工人来指导，他们也可以为十分之九的人口利益做到同样的事情……一切社会主义宣传都必须从抽象、一般改造为具体、直接实用；没收银行，依靠群众，为他们利益去完成德国武器与弹药供应局（W.U.M.B.A.）正在德国完成的事情。

The war has reaffirmed clearly enough and in a very practical way … that modern capitalist society, particularly in the advanced countries, has fully matured for the transition to socialism. If, for instance, Germany can direct the economic life of 66 million people from a single, central institution … then the same can be done, in the interests of nine-tenths of the population, by the non-propertied masses if their struggle is directed by the class-conscious workers…. All propaganda for socialism must be refashioned from abstract and general to concrete and directly practical; expropriate the banks and, relying on the masses, carry out in their interests the very same thing the W.U.M.B.A. [i.e., Weapons and Ammunition Supply Department] is carrying out in Germany.

zh: 截至1914年夏，有两种潜在的历史逻辑在争夺俄国的未来，一种是自由主义，另一种是社会主义。然而两者都许诺这个国家将获得“西方”命运。因此，关于1917年革命的大问题便是：为什么，在颠倒欧洲通常的历史优先次序的情况下，社会主义逻辑胜出了？为什么结果变得如此专制而“东方”？或者反过来问：为什么自由主义逻辑被证明如此脆弱——也就是说，俄国究竟有没有机会避免布尔什维主义？
en: As of the summer of 1914, two potential logics of history were contending for Russia’s future, the one liberal and the other socialist. Both, however, promised a “Western” destiny for the country. So the great question about the Revolution of 1917 is this: Why, in a reversal of the usual European order of historical priorities, did the socialist logic win out, and why did the result turn out to be so despotic and “Oriental”? Or, to put the matter the other way around: Why did the liberal logic prove to be so weak—that is, did Russia ever stand a chance of avoiding Bolshevism?

zh: 正是问题的第二种提法，从革命爆发之时直到斯大林去世之后，一直居于史学关切的核心——在那个时期，流亡的俄国自由派及其西方同道主导着关于十月意义的争论。只是随着斯大林去世和赫鲁晓夫的改革，布尔什维主义本身能否走一条更自由、“西方”的道路——一条通向“具有人道面孔的社会主义”的道路——才成为主导争论的问题。本章将顺着这一史学演进的轨迹，考察如今已被忽视的自由主义问题；共产主义实现自由化的潜力问题，则留待后面几章处理。不过，本节的目的并不是哀叹那条未被走过的路；而是更清楚地揭示，现实中为什么走了另一条路。一切历史研究都包含“本来可能如何”的成分，因为历史行动者实际上正是通过以替代可能性衡量现实，来作出自己的选择。
en: It is this second formulation of the question that was at the center of historiographical concern from the time of the Revolution itself until after Stalin’s death—a period when émigré Russian liberals and their Western counterparts dominated the debate about the meaning of October. It was only with Stalin’s death and Khrushchev’s reforms that the question of how Bolshevism itself might have taken a more liberal, “Western” course—one leading to “socialism with a human face”—came to dominate the debate. Following in the traces of this historiographical progression, the present chapter will explore the now-neglected liberal question; the question of Communism’s potential for liberalization will be treated in later chapters. The purpose of the present exercise, however, is not to lament the road not taken; rather, it is to bring out more clearly why, in reality, an alternative route was followed. All historical investigation entails a component of the might-have-been, for assessing reality in terms of alternative possibilities is the way that historical actors in fact make their choices.

zh: 自由主义论证的要旨是：从1860年代亚历山大二世的“大改革”，到1905年后国家杜马治下的“立宪实验”，俄国一直在朝西方式的宪政民主演变，而这里的西方模式是由英国和法国、而不是由德国和奥地利界定的。据此，1905—1906年的宪法被视为一间中转站，或一段学徒期，通向充分的政治现代性。这将是俄国的西化逻辑，是她对欧洲共同命运的最终实现。这一论证的一个重要推论是：首相彼得·斯托雷平同时推行的农业改革，如果再有二十年左右的时间发挥作用，本可以解决俄国的农民问题，从而为民主秩序提供社会基础。因为这些改革旨在拆解古老的农民村社，将其变为个人持有的土地，从而创造一个更繁荣、更稳定的乡村——“押注于强者与清醒者”，斯托雷平如是说。在这种自由主义观点看来，俄国最终未能兑现其西化承诺，是因为第一次世界大战这一“意外”。这场战争把俄国仍然稚嫩的政治结构扰乱到如此地步，以至于布尔什维克党——一个倒退到1870年代暴烈密谋政治的产物——得以在1917年的“十月政变”中夺取政权。于是俄国错过了民主的机会，重新陷入比以往所知的任何专制都更糟糕的专制。
en: The essence of the liberal argument is that from the Great Reforms of Alexander II in the 1860s, down through the “constitutional experiment” under the State Duma after 1905, Russia was evolving towards a constitutional democracy on the Western model, as that model was defined by Britain and France rather than by Germany and Austria. Accordingly, the constitution of 1905-1906 was viewed as a halfway house, or an apprenticeship, on the way to full political modernity. This was to be Russia’s Westernizing logic, her final realization of a common European destiny. A major corollary to this argument is that the concurrent agrarian reforms of Prime Minister Petr Stolypin, if they had had twenty or so more years to work, would have solved Russia’s peasant problem and thus would have provided a social foundation for a democratic order. For these reforms were designed to break up the archaic peasant commune into individual holdings and so create a more prosperous and stable countryside—“a wager on the strong and the sober,” as Stolypin put it. In this liberal view, Russia eventually fell short of her Westernizing promise because of the “accident” of the First World War. This war disorganized Russia’s still immature political structures to the point where the Bolshevik Party, a throwback to the violent and conspiratorial politics of the 1870s, was able to seize power in the “October coup” of 1917. Thus Russia missed her chance for democracy and relapsed into a despotism far worse than any she had known in the past.

zh: 自由主义观点提出了三个历史解释的根本问题。第一，在立宪实验之下、在第一次世界大战的冲击之前，俄国实现民主的机会究竟有多大？第二，在1917年2月君主制垮台之后、身处战争之中，她的机会又有多大？第三，在决定民主失败和布尔什维主义胜利的过程中，国内社会发展因素与外部战争冲击各自起了多大比例的作用？只有在这三个问题的脉络中，才有可能处理布尔什维主义本身的性质以及十月合法性这两组问题。
en: The liberal view raises three fundamental questions of historical interpretation. First, how good were Russia’s chances for democracy under the constitutional experiment and before the shock of the First World War? Second, how good were her chances after the fall of the monarchy in February 1917, in the midst of that war? Third, in what proportions were the factors of internal social development and the impact of external war instrumental in determining the failure of democracy and the victory of Bolshevism? Only in the context of these three questions is it possible to grapple with the problems of the nature of Bolshevism itself and of the legitimacy of October.

zh: 通往二月站
en: TO THE FEBRUARY STATION

zh: 1905年产生的伪立宪主义政治大厦，其性质与脆弱之处前文已经描述。但这一制度在截至1914年的那些年份里所依托的社会环境又如何呢？只有考察这一环境，我们才能回答刚才提出的三个宽泛的解释问题。
en: The nature and the vulnerabilities of the political edifice of pseudoconstitutionalism that emerged from 1905 have already been described. But what of the social setting in which that system operated in the years down to 1914? It is only by examining that setting that we can answer the three broad questions of interpretation just posed.

zh: 到立宪实验之时，俄罗斯帝国的人口已达到约一亿七千万。其中约80%是农民。大约15%的农民拥有脱离村社的个体地产，而50%以上仍生活在完整的村社之中。此外，俄罗斯中部诸省人口过剩，居民就业不足；农民认为，可以通过没收仍掌握在贵族和国家手中的土地来补救这一状况。尽管这种设想事实上是错误的，农民“土地饥渴”仍然是俄国生活中一股强大的力量。简言之，到1917年，斯托雷平的农业改革还没有时间从根本上改变俄国乡村，乡村相对于乡间贵族而言，仍是重大不稳定的来源。
en: By the time of the constitutional experiment, the population of the Russian Empire had reached approximately one hundred seventy million. Of these, some 80 percent were peasants. Approximately 15 percent of the peasants had individual land holdings separate from the commune, while more than 50 percent still lived in full-fledged communes. Furthermore, the Central Russian provinces were overpopulated and their inhabitants underemployed, a situation the peasants thought could be remedied through the confiscation of lands that remained in the hands of the gentry and the state. Though this supposition was in fact false, peasant “land hunger” was nonetheless a potent force in Russian life. In short, as of 1917 Stolypin’s agrarian reforms had not had the time to change the Russian countryside fundamentally, and it remained a source of major instability vis-à-vis the gentry of the country.

zh: 俄国直到十九世纪末才第一次拥有一个由相当规模城市组成的网络。圣彼得堡的人口在1897年突破百万，莫斯科五年后的1902年也达到同一数字；到1917年，两座城市的人口都已增至略多于两百万。总体而言，到1914年，帝国计有一千万至一千二百万城市居民，其中大多数是各种层次的中产阶级，或不同级别的国家职员。产业工人有三百万至三百五十万，此外还有一百万铁路系统雇员。是否把产业工人和铁路雇员称为无产阶级，是一个政治和意识形态问题；但就实际情况而言，他们的物质处境十分边缘，组织权利也受到限制。因此，无论政权还是革命政党，都把工人视为“危险”分子，尤其是考虑到他们集中于大城市和关键交通动脉。这样，俄国的新城市就在旧乡村所提供的激进人群之外，又增添了第二支激进队伍。
en: It was only in the late nineteenth century that Russia for the first time had a network of sizeable cities. St. Petersburg’s population passed the million mark in 1897, Moscow’s did the same five years later in 1902; by 1917 the population of each city had grown to somewhat more than two million. Overall, the Empire counted some ten million to twelve million urban residents by 1914, most of them middle class, at various levels, or state functionaries of diverse rank. Industrial workers numbered from three million to three and one-half million, and in addition there were one million employees of the railroad system. Whether or not one calls these latter groups the proletariat is a question of politics and ideology, but as a practical matter their material situation was marginal and their right to organize limited. The workers were therefore regarded by both the regime and the revolutionary parties as “dangerous” elements, especially in view of their concentration in large urban centers and along key arteries of communication. Thus Russia’s new cities added a second radical cohort to that furnished by her old villages.

zh: 这些众所周知的基本事实，常常被陈述得仿佛十月革命会从它们之中通过自发的社会燃烧自动产生。但在整个二十世纪，从巴西到韩国，快速工业化的国家中都存在过类似的社会不稳定局面，却都没有产生马克思主义革命。的确，在一亿七千万总人口中，约三百万“无产者”很难构成足以支撑人类第一次从资本主义跃向社会主义这样重大事业的强大社会基础。显然，必定还有其他因素在起作用，而这些因素不是社会和经济因素，而是政治和意识形态因素。
en: These well-known basic facts are often set forth as if the October Revolution would automatically arise from them by spontaneous social combustion. But throughout the twentieth century, situations of comparable social instability have existed in rapidly industrializing countries—from Brazil to South Korea—without producing Marxist revolutions. Indeed, around 3 million “proletarians” out of a total population of 170 million is hardly an impressive social base for so momentous an undertaking as the world’s first leap from capitalism to socialism. Clearly, other factors must have been involved in producing this result, and these factors were not social and economic but, rather, political and ideological.

zh: 第一个政治因素，是1905年建立的宪政秩序并不完整。它不再是军事专制，也还不是宪政民主，而是一种本质上不稳定的妥协，迟早必须让位：主权终有一天必须明确地归于人民或民族，因为自十七世纪以来，欧洲其他地方代议制机构的势头一直如此。但在那些例子里，这一转变需要大量时间，并经历一连串政治动荡。英国用了四十八年——从1640年到1688年——才用立宪寡头制稀释了绝对君主制，然后又度过漫长的十九世纪，才加上普选权。法国从1789年到1875年，才从绝对君主制走向持久的普选共和国。美国在这一模式中是突出的例外，因为正如托克维尔所说，“它没有经历革命的过程，却得到了革命的果实”，
或者如美国人自己所说，他们“生而自由”。撇开北欧和西欧那些成功的小国不谈，我们可以注意到，德国、意大利和日本直到在第二次世界大战中战败之后，才成为稳定的普选民主国家。
en: The first political factor is the incompleteness of the constitutional order created in 1905. No longer a military autocracy and not yet a constitutional democracy, this order was an inherently unstable compromise that sooner or later had to give way: Sovereignty would one day have to devolve clearly on the people or the nation, for this had been the momentum of representative institutions elsewhere in Europe since the seventeenth century. But in these cases the transition had required a great deal of time and a succession of political upheavals. It took England forty-eight years—from 1640 to 1688—to dilute absolute monarchy with a constitutional oligarchy, and then a long nineteenth century to add universal suffrage. France required the years 1789-1875 to move from absolute monarchy to an enduring republic with universal suffrage. The United States is an outstanding exception in this pattern because, as Tocqueville said, “it arrived at the fruits of revolution without having to go through the process,”

or, as the Americans said of themselves, they were “born free.” Leaving aside the successful smaller nations of Northern and Western Europe, we can note that Germany, Italy, and Japan did not become stable universal-suffrage democracies until after their defeat in the Second World War.

zh: 因此，对大多数现代民族而言，通往宪政民主的道路漫长、崎岖而曲折。在这一比较视野中，即便承认二十世纪一切事情都比十七世纪运转得更快，仍然需要极大的信念，才能相信俄国仅仅持续十二年的立宪实验，在没有进一步革命事变的情况下，有合理前景达到其民主目标。
en: Thus the road to constitutional democracy has been long, rocky, and tortuous for most modern nations. In this comparative perspective, and even granting that in the twentieth century everything moves faster than it did in the seventeenth, it still requires a major act of faith to believe that the Russian constitutional experiment of only twelve-years duration had reasonable prospects of attaining its democratic goal short of further revolutionary incidents.

zh: 的确，1912年之后，俄国的社会和政治局势都再次升温，酝酿着一场新的危机，将第二次让政权与社会对立起来。自由主义要求真正宪法的鼓动重新兴起；工人斗争重新活跃——这一次是在社会主义而非自由主义领导下；农民则像世纪初以来那样，仍心怀不满、感到疏离。与此同时，斯托雷平1911年遇刺之后，专制政权越来越顽固地抵制任何进一步变革。因此，渐进变革越来越不可能，法外行动相应地越来越可能。简言之，这个国家正走向一场重大的宪政危机。鉴于沙皇尼古拉二世无意接受降格为其英国表亲那样的地位，他就必须被强迫投降或退位，而使用武力将使这场危机在某种程度上具有革命性质。
en: Indeed, after 1912 both the social and the political situations in Russia were heating up once again for a new crisis that would pit the regime against society for a second time. Liberal agitation for a real constitution resumed; worker militancy revived—this time under socialist rather than liberal leadership; and the peasantry remained as sullenly alienated as it had been since the beginning of the century. Concurrently, after Stolypin’s assassination in 1911, the autocracy increasingly dug in its heels against any further change. An evolutionary transformation was therefore increasingly unlikely, and extralegal action was correspondingly more probable. In short, the country was headed towards a major constitutional crisis. Given the fact that Tsar Nicholas II had no intention of accepting demotion to the status of his British cousin, he would have to be forced to either capitulate or abdicate, and the use of force would make the crisis to some degree revolutionary.

zh: 在推测这种危机的各种情景时，关键问题是新革命会有多大。这在很大程度上取决于危机是在和平时期到来，还是像1905年那样在战争期间到来；如果是后者，还取决于那是怎样一场战争。我们知道，危机事实上是在一场空前毁灭性的战争中途到来的。但假如是和平时期的第二次俄国革命，它会是什么样子？关于这个问题，我们所能说的少量内容，只能从我们对1917年实际发生之事以及其他欧洲和平时期革命案例的了解中推断。
en: In speculating on the various scenarios for such a crisis, the key question is how big would the new revolution be. This would largely depend on whether the crisis came in peacetime or, as in 1905, during a war, and, if the latter, on what sort of war. As we know, the crisis in fact came in the midst of a uniquely devastating war. But what might a peacetime second Russian revolution have looked like? What little we can say on this subject must be extrapolated from what we know of what actually happened in 1917 and from other cases of peacetime revolution in Europe.

zh: 然而，在这段简短的反事实历史插叙的开头，有两件事几乎可以确定。第一，无论在和平还是战争时期，像俄国1914年那样的局势只有三种可能结局：要么宪政民主在第一轮获胜；要么社会主义左派夺取政权；要么君主制和右派恢复秩序。第二，革命按其本性使立宪主义者处于极大劣势；因为立宪主义按其本性，与暴力和法外手段不相容。因此，无论需要多少法外手段来迫使君主制屈服或将其摧毁，这些手段也都有发展出自己的势头并失控的风险。但这个困境绝非俄国独有：1640年的英国议会和1789年的法国三级会议面临完全相同的困境，而两者都在第一轮把立宪主义的战斗输给了一个强人。立宪主义者似乎不得不等到第二轮，才能迎来自己的时代。
en: Yet at the outset of this brief excursus into counterfactual history, it is possible to say two things with near certainty. First, whether in peace or in war, there are only three possible outcomes to a situation such as Russia’s in 1914: Either constitutional democracy wins out in the first round; or the socialist Left seizes power; or the monarchy and the Right restore order. Second, revolution, by its very nature, puts the constitutionalists at a major disadvantage; for constitutionalism, by its nature, is incompatible with violence and extralegal means. Thus, whatever measure of extralegality proves to be necessary to bend or break the monarchy also entails the risk of developing its own momentum and getting out of hand. But this dilemma is by no means peculiar to Russia: The English Parliament in 1640, and the French Estates General in 1789, faced exactly the same dilemma, and both lost the battle for constitutionalism in the first round to a strongman. Constitutionalists, it seems, have to wait until the second round to have their day.

zh: “温和”英国革命失败的一个原因，当然在于它并不是一场和平时期的革命：它由对苏格兰的有限战争引发，随后又因爱尔兰一场更严重的战争而激进化。但即便是和平时期革命的例子也不令人鼓舞。法国革命始于和平时期，但不到两年就生成了一场国际战争，后者又导致内战和国内的普遍激进化。1848年革命同样在和平时期爆发，虽然远不如1789年革命激进，却仍然处处以建立威权政府告终。这在很大程度上是因为，在法国如同在奥地利和普鲁士一样，占多数的农民最终支持恢复秩序，从而孤立了激进的城市下层阶级；这一模式将在1871年由战争催生的巴黎公社身上以更剧烈的形式重演。
en: One reason for the failure of the “moderate” English revolution is that it was not, of course, a peacetime revolution: It was triggered by limited war with Scotland, and then radicalized by a more serious war in Ireland. But even the examples of peacetime revolutions are not encouraging. The French Revolution began in peacetime, but within two years it generated an international war that then led to civil war and general radicalization at home. The revolutions of 1848 also broke out in peacetime, and though hardly as radical as that of 1789 they nonetheless ended everywhere with the establishment of authoritarian governments. This is in large part because, in France no less than in Austria and Prussia, the peasant majority eventually supported the restoration of order, thus isolating the radical urban lower classes, a pattern which would be repeated in more drastic form in the case of the war-engendered Paris Commune in 1871.

zh: 俄国当然是一个压倒性的农民国家，而她的农民是激进的——像1789年的法国农民，而不像1848年或1871年的法国农民。在任何一场和平时期的俄国革命中，农民都一定会要求并得到土地，因为就连立宪民主党人（卡德特）也想把土地让给他们，并向贵族支付补偿，而社会主义者则想直接交出土地，正如1917年实际发生的那样。不过，即便在和平时期，这样的转移也会带来一场巨大、突兀、很可能混乱的剧变，并伴随相应的内乱风险。一个新选出的立宪会议，能比1789年法国国民议会处理“大恐慌”和八月四日之夜更顺利地处理这件事吗？一个俄国临时政府会如何应对一场仿照1848年巴黎六月起义或1905年12月莫斯科起义的城市暴动？它又会如何回应不可避免的新的波兰起义和独立宣言？
en: Russia, of course, was an overwhelmingly peasant country, and her peasantry was radical—like that of France in 1789, but unlike that of France in 1848 or 1871. In any peacetime Russian revolution, the peasants would certainly have demanded and received the land, for even the Constitutional Democrats (Kadets) wanted to cede it to them with reimbursement to the gentry, and the socialists wanted to surrender it outright, as in fact happened in 1917. Still, even in peacetime such a transfer would have entailed an enormous, brusque, and probably disorderly upheaval with a corresponding potential for civil strife. Could a newly elected Constituent Assembly have managed this more smoothly than the French National Assembly of 1789 managed the Grande Peur and the night of August 4? How would a Russian Provisional Government have met an urban insurrection on the model of the Parisian June Days of 1848 or the Moscow uprising of December 1905? How would it have reacted to the inevitable new Polish insurrection and declaration of independence?

zh: 我们显然不知道。但任何新政府对这些问题及其他问题的反应，在很大程度上将取决于农民在得到土地之后多快“去激进化”，而一旦欧洲农民成为自己的主人，历来都是如此。正是这一因素尤其会决定任何城市暴动的命运，因为在一个人口以农业为主的国家，只要农民支持政府，工人起义就不可能成功。在这种情况下，社会主义起义只会把国家推向右边，结果可能类似于另一场和平时期革命，即1930年代的西班牙。
en: We obviously do not know. But any new government’s reaction to these and other problems would have been largely conditioned by how quickly the peasantry “deradicalized” itself after receiving the land, as has always been the case for European peasantries once they have become their own masters. It is this factor in particular that would determine the fortunes of any urban insurrection, for a worker revolt in a largely agrarian country could not succeed if the peasantry supported the government. In such a case, a socialist insurrection would only push the country to the right, and the outcome might resemble that of another peacetime revolution, that of Spain in the 1930s.

zh: 但无论我们怎样想象一场和平时期的俄国革命，最不可能的结果都是红色十月。社会史学家曾颇有道理地论证，城市暴动是1914年罢工浪潮的一种潜在可能，而和平时期的危机十有八九会产生一场实际革命。

但即便如此，也完全不等同于布尔什维克党夺取政权并建立一个持久的“工人国家”，也不等同于布尔什维克无限期地行使权力，推行镇压市场、将整个经济国有化的最大化纲领。任何这种长期的“建设社会主义”，在和平时期的牌局中都几乎不可能出现。1914年那个炎热夏天更可能的结果，是一场流产的工人起义、宪政民主的失败，以及一个民族保守主义政权——两次大战之间的欧洲屡见不鲜的那种政权。但这样的政权，无论其政治多么残暴，至少会保留市场、私有财产和市民社会的基本要素——正如佛朗哥的西班牙那样。
en: But no matter how we imagine a peacetime Russian revolution, the least likely outcome would be a Red October. Social historians have argued with some plausibility that an urban insurrection was a potentiality of the strike wave of 1914, and that in all probability a peacetime crisis would have produced an actual revolution.

But this would not have been at all the same as a Bolshevik Party seizure of power leading to an enduring “workers’ state” nor would it have been the same as an indefinite Bolshevik exercise of power with a maximalist program of suppressing the market and nationalizing the entire economy. Any such long-term “building of socialism” was hardly in the peacetime cards. A far more likely outcome of the hot summer of 1914 would have been an abortive workers’ revolt, the failure of constitutional democracy, and a national conservative regime of the sort that interwar Europe saw all too often. But such a regime, however brutal its politics may have been, would at least have preserved the market, private property, and the fundamentals of a civil society—as did Franco’s Spain.

zh: 因此，回答我们的第一个问题，我们可以得出结论：如果俄国得以免遭第一次世界大战的冲击，她要有机而和平地演变为宪政民主，近乎需要奇迹。
然而，即便是在和平时期最坏的情景——一个民族保守主义政权——她的境况也会远好于那场战争实际给她带来的结果。
en: So in answer to our first question, we may conclude that it would have required a near miracle for Russia to have evolved organically and peacefully into a constitutional democracy had she been spared the shock of the First World War.
Yet even in the worst-case peacetime scenario of a national conservative regime, she would have fared far better than she in fact did as a result of that war.

zh: 但俄国和欧洲要避免这样一场战争，同样近乎需要另一个奇迹。五个主要大国分成两个紧密同盟，对峙于毕竟只是地球上最小的大陆。每个国家都武装到牙齿；除英国外，所有国家都拥有以普遍兵役制为基础的大规模“民主”军队，这种社会军事化程度在历史上从未有过（英国很快也不得不效仿）；所有大国都有一旦启动就几乎无法停止的动员时间表；每个大国又都对其他大国承担着同样具有约束力的军事义务。
en: But it would have required another near miracle for Russia and Europe to have avoided such a war. Five major powers were arrayed in two tight alliances on what is, after all, the planet’s smallest continent. Each power was armed to the hilt; all except Great Britain had mass “democratic” armies based on universal military service, a degree of social militarization never before realized in history (and one that Britain would soon have to imitate); all the powers had mobilization schedules that, once started, were almost impossible to stop; and each had equally constraining military commitments to other powers.

zh: 然而同样重要的是，没有一个主要大国知道现代战争究竟是什么样子；每个国家都以1866年持续七周的普奥战争为参照，或者最坏也不过以1870—1871年持续六个月的普法战争为参照，而后者实际上只有八周的实际交战。因此，所有交战方——俄国也许是其中最极端的例子——都轻率地设想了一场全欧冲突，却没有意识到它有可能摧毁它们的国内政权和整个欧洲秩序。脱离这一始终存在的威胁，去抽象地推论俄国二十世纪初的社会极化，是徒劳的；因为如果萨拉热窝事件没有触发那场洪水，那么几乎可以肯定，稍后某个事件也会触发它。
en: Just as important, however, none of the major powers knew what modern war was really like; each thought in terms of the seven-week Austro-Prussian War of 1866 or, at the worst, in terms of the six-month Franco-Prussian War of 1870-1871, during which there were, in fact, only eight weeks of active combat. Thus all the belligerents—with Russia perhaps being the most extreme example—carelessly contemplated a general European conflict without realizing its potential for destroying their domestic regimes and the whole European order. It is futile to reason about Russia’s early twentieth-century social polarization in abstraction from this ever present threat, for if the incident at Sarajevo had not triggered the deluge, in all probability some slightly later incident would have done so.

zh: 事实上，1914年之后，战争把当时正在聚集的第二次俄国革命的性质彻底改变了，使这个国家内部进程的逻辑从属于残暴事件的“外在”偶然性。关于1917年二月至十月间的发展，首先要指出的特征是：第二次俄国革命的进程“险恶、残酷而短促”。从俄国旧政权垮台到布尔什维克宣布世界上第一个社会主义政府，中间只隔了八个月，这种历史的压缩在欧洲革命编年史上没有先例。
en: As it in fact turned out, after 1914 the war radically altered the nature of the then-gathering second Russian Revolution by subordinating the logic of the country’s internal processes to the “extraneous” contingency of brute events. The first characteristic to note about developments between February and October 1917 is that the course of the Second Russian Revolution was “nasty, brutish, and short.” Only eight months separated the fall of the Russian Old Regime from the Bolsheviks’ proclamation of the world’s first socialist government, a telescoping of history without precedent in the annals of European revolutions.

zh: 这种加速的原因，在于欧洲生活中另一件史无前例的事情：世界上第一场“总体战”，这是这场战争的主要实践者之一埃里希·冯·鲁登道夫将军的说法。
第一次，欧洲各交战国都动员全体人口，成效各有不同：人们或是到前线参战，或是在后方劳动支援。正常政治被中止，经济被国有化和军事化，文化被转为宣传，私人生活被公共目的遮蔽。没有哪个国家的社会秩序能在这种侵入下原封不动地幸存，而脆弱、摇晃的俄国尤其不可能。她的经济、社会和政治制度，都与1914年时相比发生了根本转变。
en: The cause of this acceleration lay in an equally unprecedented occurrence in European life: the world’s first “total war,” as one of its prime practitioners, General Erich von Ludendorff, called it.

For the first time, in each of the belligerent nations of Europe and with one or another degree of success, the whole of the population was mobilized either to participate in the conflict at the front or to work to support it in the rear. Normal politics were suspended, the economy was nationalized and militarized, culture was turned to propaganda, and private life was eclipsed by public purpose. No nation’s social order could survive such intrusion unaltered, and that of fragile, rickety Russia least of all. Her economy, her society, and her political system alike were radically transformed from what they had been in 1914.

zh: 首先，在战争过程中，约有一千一百万俄国男子被动员，其中八百万人——相当于圣彼得堡和莫斯科人口总和的两倍——到1917年时，沿着从波罗的海到黑海约两千英里的战线展开。此外，到1917年，这支力量已遭受约三百万人的伤亡，绝对数字超过任何其他交战国。所有幸存者都已习惯于把暴力当作生活方式。然而这些巨大的人员牺牲似乎毫无用处：三年来，帝国军队从一个失败走向另一个失败，到1917年已失去帝国西部诸省的很大一部分。
en: First of all, some eleven million Russian men were mobilized in the course of the hostilities, and eight million of these, or twice the populations of St. Petersburg and Moscow combined, as of 1917 were strung out along the roughly two-thousand-mile front from the Baltic to the Black Sea. Furthermore, as of 1917 this force had suffered some three million casualties, more in absolute terms than any other belligerent nation. And all of the survivors had become accustomed to violence as a way of life. Yet these enormous human sacrifices seemed to have been made without avail: For three years the Imperial army went from defeat to defeat, and by 1917 it had lost a significant portion of the Empire’s western provinces.

zh: 此外，如此庞大的人口从劳动力中被抽走，大大加剧了经济的混乱，而其他因素原已削弱了经济。首先，同盟国对俄国波罗的海和黑海港口的封锁，终结了她的粮食和原材料出口，使她失去主要收入；封锁也终止了所需工业设备和消费品的进口。结果，这个国家充斥着粮食，而由于消费品匮乏，农民几乎没有出售的积极性，城市于是开始经历严重短缺。与此同时，战争努力垄断了运输、工业和燃料，进一步减少了对城市平民的供应。再者，在收入下降的情况下，政府靠印钞来应付战争的额外开支，从而开启了本世纪第一场大通胀，而整体经济中供给相对于需求的稀缺又加剧了这一状况。最后，帝国政府比其它交战国的政府更不向现代商业利益开放，在组织战时经济方面效率也低得多；这同样加剧了这个国家的分裂倾向。
en: The removal of so huge a mass from the labor force, moreover, contributed significantly to the disorganization of an economy that was already being undermined by other factors. First, the blockade of Russia’s Baltic and Black Sea ports by the Central Powers ended her export of grain and raw materials and deprived her of major revenues; this blockade also ended the import of needed industrial equipment and consumer goods. As a result, the country was glutted with foodstuffs that the peasants had little incentive to sell because of the dearth of consumer goods, and the cities consequently began to experience severe scarcities. At the same time, the war effort monopolized transport, industry, and fuel, further diminishing supplies to the civilian population of the cities. In addition, in the face of decreased revenues, the government met the exceptional expenses of the war by printing money, thereby inaugurating this century’s first great inflation, a condition aggravated by the scarcity of supply vis-à-vis demand in the economy as a whole. Finally, the Imperial government, less open to modern business interests than the governments of the other belligerent powers, was far less effective in organizing the economy for war; this, too, aggravated the country’s fissiparous tendencies.

zh: 与此同时，在政治战线上，1905—1906年的半宪法实际上被中止了。
在任何战争中，行政权相对于立法权和司法权总会得到加强；但在俄国，这一过程走得远比其它交战国更远。由于尼古拉从未真正接受专制权力被稀释，他抓住军事紧急状态，几乎不召开杜马就进行统治——因此也得不到自由派反对派为战争努力所提供的支持。这一政策，加上拉斯普京的得势及其对皇后亚历山德拉的影响（尼古拉在前线期间，实际上由她治理），在反对派看来就像一场针对宪政秩序的政变。
en: On the political front, meanwhile, the semiconstitution of 1905-1906 was virtually suspended.

In any war the executive power is always strengthened vis-à-vis the legislative and the judicial; but in Russia this process went much further than in the other belligerent countries. Because Nicholas had never really accepted the dilution of autocracy, he seized on the military emergency to rule almost without convening the Duma—and thus also without the support that the liberal opposition offered for the war effort. This policy, in conjunction with the ascendancy of Rasputin and his influence over Empress Alexandra, who in effect governed while Nicholas was away at the front, looked to the opposition like a coup d’état against the constitutional order.

zh: 因此，自由派反对派在杜马中组建进步联盟，采取了近似反政变的行动。这个联盟从立宪民主党人一直到温和保守派，要求建立一个享有国民信任的政府——这一让步实际上等于一部真正的宪法。于是，一场宪政危机在一场失败的战争中、在经济开始崩溃之际展开：只有这三种情况结合在一起，彼得格勒工人中间二月的社会不满，才能变成1917年的二月革命。
en: The liberal opposition, therefore, mounted a quasi-countercoup by forming the Progressive Bloc in the Duma. Ranging from the Kadets to the moderate conservatives, it demanded a government that would enjoy the confidence of the nation—a concession that, in effect, would have amounted to a real constitution. Thus, a constitutional crisis unfolded in the midst of a losing war and while the economy was beginning to break down: Only with the combination of these three circumstances could the social discontent of February among the Petrograd workers become the February Revolution of 1917.

zh: 这场革命是一次短暂却毁灭性的爆炸。

在该月最后几天，工人反对食品短缺的抗议升级为工业罢工，最终升级为反对战争和专制的群众政治示威。当彼得格勒由农民士兵组成的卫戍部队拒绝向人群开枪时，这些骚动就变成了一场革命，从而使政府在自己的首都失去了权力。它成为一场胜利的革命，首先是因为杜马中的进步联盟抛弃了君主制，介入组建临时政府以稳定局势；其次是因为这一篡权得到了军队最高统帅部的认可，从而迫使尼古拉退位。就这样，在五天之内，俄国旧政权没有做丝毫抵抗，就像纸牌屋一样垮掉了。
en: This Revolution came as a brief but devastating explosion.

In the last days of the month worker protests against food shortages escalated into industrial strikes, and finally into mass political demonstrations against the war and the autocracy. These disturbances became a revolution when the Petrograd garrison of peasant soldiers refused to fire on the crowds, thus depriving the government of power in its own capital. They became a victorious revolution, first, when the Progressive Bloc of the Duma abandoned the monarchy and stepped in to form a Provisional Government in an effort to stabilize the situation, and second, when this usurpation was approved by the army high command, thereby forcing Nicholas’s abdication. Thus, in five days the Russian Old Regime, without putting up the slightest resistance, collapsed like a house of cards.

zh: 尽管这一过程的触发者是首都的工人阶级，但决定性的革命行动者却是穿上军装的农民，因为正是他的拒绝服从使帝国政府失去了效力。然而应当强调，他的动机主要不是与工人的社会团结——尽管这一因素当然存在——而是对战争的厌恶。但如果没有宪政危机，就连这场哗变也不足以造成革命。因为权力顶端的瘫痪意味着，无论是信誉扫地的国家权威，还是缺乏组织的反对派，都找不到抵抗街头爆发的意志或手段。这种无能的结果，是一切公共权威的瓦解，从警察到地方行政机构，全都干脆消失了。正是二月崩溃的这种彻底性，决定了接替已死旧政权的临时政府为何如此无能。
en: Although the trigger in this process was the working class of the capital, the decisive revolutionary agent was the peasant in uniform, for it was his refusal to obey that neutralized the Imperial government. It should be emphasized, however, that his motivation was not primarily social solidarity with the workers—although this factor was of course present—but revulsion against the war. Yet even this mutiny would not have sufficed to make a revolution had it not been for the constitutional crisis. For the paralysis of power at the top meant that neither a discredited state authority nor an unorganized opposition could find the will or the means to resist the eruption of the street. The result of this impotence was the unraveling of all public authority, from the police to the local administration, both of which simply melted away. It is this completeness of the February collapse that determined the impotence of the Provisional Government that succeeded the defunct Old Regime.

zh: 新政府由杜马中的进步联盟组成，最初由立宪民主党人主导。但从一开始，这个政府就是工人和士兵的人质，正是他们的哗变才使它得以掌权。而且，这些力量立即被社会主义知识分子组织成一个工人和士兵代表委员会，即苏维埃。此外，在二月事变期间，这个苏维埃还发布了著名的“第一号命令”，使军队民主化；这一措施实际上使军官团失去作用，从而削弱了新政府对武装力量的控制。因此，临时政府根本算不上一个政府，而只是一个临时行政机构；它能否运作，取决于苏维埃的善意，而苏维埃表达的是工人和士兵“群众”对“资产阶级”和“资本主义”内阁的不信任。
en: The new government was formed by the Progressive Bloc of the Duma and was initially dominated by the Kadets. But from the outset this government was the hostage of the workers and soldiers whose mutiny had permitted it to come to power. These forces, moreover, were immediately organized by socialist intellectuals into a Council, or Soviet, of Workers’ and Soldiers’ Deputies. In addition, amidst the February events this Soviet issued its famous “Order Number One” democratizing the army, a measure which had the effect of neutralizing the officer corps and thus undermining the new government’s control over its armed forces. The Provisional Government was therefore no government at all, but a mere provisional administration; its ability to function was dependent on the goodwill of the Soviet, which expressed the distrust of the worker and soldier “masses” toward the “bourgeois” and “capitalist” ministry.

zh: 通往十月终点站
en: TO THE OCTOBER TERMINUS

zh: 这种权力分立、猜疑制度化的体制，被称为“双重政权”。很快就显而易见，这样的制度本质上不稳定，因此不可避免地会以两种权力中的一个消灭另一个而告终。从这种局面中必然发展出那场常常被描绘成史诗的“资产阶级”临时政府与社会主义苏维埃之间的政治斗争。
en: This system of divided authority and institutionalized suspicion has been called a regime of “dual power.” It soon became apparent that such a system was intrinsically unstable and hence would inevitably end with one of the two powers eliminating the other. Out of this situation necessarily developed the political struggle, so often portrayed in epic terms, between the “bourgeois” Provisional Government and the socialist Soviet.

zh: 从二月到十月这八个月的著名故事，分为四个阶段。第一阶段从二月到四月，当时占主导的立宪民主党人试图搁置任何进一步的激进变革，以便集中精力赢得战争。这一主战政策在四月引发危机，苏维埃中的孟什维克和社会革命党人迫使临时政府采取更“民主”、纯粹“防御性”的军事立场。但作为交换，他们不得不同立宪民主党人一起进入政府，从而把充当强硬左翼反对派的角色让给了布尔什维克。正是在这个恰当的时机，列宁回到国内，并在他的《四月提纲》中使他此前举棋不定的党接受了一套纲领：“结束战争”、“打倒临时政府”、“全部政权归苏维埃”。
en: The well-known story of the eight months separating February from October falls into four phases. The first extended from February to April, a time when the dominant Kadets sought to adjourn any further radical change in order to concentrate on winning the war. This prowar policy produced in April a crisis in which the Mensheviks and SRs in the Soviet forced the Provisional Government to adopt a more “democratic” and purely “defensist” military stance. But in exchange they had to enter the government alongside the Kadets, thereby abandoning the role of hard-Left opposition to the Bolsheviks. It was at this timely juncture that Lenin arrived home and, in his April Theses, converted his hitherto confused Party to a program of “down with the war,” “down with the Provisional Government,” and “all power to the Soviets.”

zh: 第二阶段从四月危机延伸到七月事变。这一时期的特点是革命迅速深化：新任社会主义国防部长亚历山大·克伦斯基堂吉诃德式地试图发动一场“民主攻势”，以展示新生俄国的活力，从而把所有交战国拉到谈判桌前。然而，这一政策唯一的受益者是布尔什维克，他们的宣传从一次成功走向另一次成功。但在七月初，他们因一次含糊的夺权尝试而用力过猛，被政府中的其他社会主义者不甚坚决地镇压下去；结果，列宁不得不躲藏起来，直到十月。
en: The second phase extended from the April Crisis to the July Days. This period was marked by a rapid deepening of the Revolution as the new socialist Defense Minister, Aleksandr Kerenskii, quixotically attempted to mount a “democratic offensive” to demonstrate the vitality of reborn Russia and thereby bring all the belligerent powers to the negotiating table. The only beneficiaries of this policy, however, were the Bolsheviks, who went from one propaganda success to another. In early July, however, they overreached themselves with an ambiguous try for power and were half-heartedly put down by their fellow governmental socialists; consequently, Lenin had to go into hiding until October.

zh: 布尔什维克的这一挫折，开启了延续到夏末的第三阶段。正如人们所料，四月至六月的左倾浪潮，在七月至八月产生了右倾浪潮。这股反作用力试图结束双重政权、镇压苏维埃、继续战争；因此它恰如其分地把焦点放在一位将军、总司令拉夫尔·科尔尼洛夫身上。这一阶段以他八月底那次含糊夺权的惨败告终——这一事件表明，俄国右派只是一个吓唬人的怪物，没有任何真正的力量。
en: This setback for the Bolsheviks inaugurated a third phase extending to the end of the summer. As was only to be expected, the left-ward surge of April—June produced a rightward surge in July—August. This reactive thrust sought to end dual power, suppress the Soviet, and get on with the war; and so it appropriately focused on a general, the commander in chief Lavr Kornilov. It ended with the fiasco of his equivocal try for power at the end of August—an event which demonstrated that the Russian Right was a mere bogeyman, without any real strength.

zh: 这一情况为左派大开方便之门，从而产生延续到十月的第四阶段。在这些秋天的月份里，由克伦斯基担任总理的临时政府不过是一个幽灵。列宁的布尔什维克于是可以自由接管“双重政权”的下半部分，即苏维埃。他们以苏维埃为行动基地，公开组织起来，要把临时政府——用列昂·托洛茨基那句著名的话说——扔进历史的垃圾箱。
en: This circumstance opened the doors wide to the Left, thus yielding a fourth phase extending to October. During these autumnal months, the Provisional Government—now presided over by Kerenskii—was no more than a phantom. Lenin’s Bolsheviks were therefore free to take over the nether half of the “dual power,” the Soviet. Using it as a base of operations, they openly organized to cast the Provisional Government, as Leon Trotsky famously put it, into the trash can of history.

zh: 这场所谓的十月革命，是由党利用彼得格勒苏维埃的机构实施的一场“武装起义”。
列宁坚持权力的转移要采取这种军事化形式，而不是采取由即将召开的全俄苏维埃代表大会投票的政治形式；后者是他那些更务实的同事格里戈里·季诺维也夫和列夫·加米涅夫所赞成的路线。他这样做，是因为对他而言，正如对马克思而言，阶级斗争字面意义上就是阶级战争，必然涉及实际的暴力。没有其他方法能充分展示真正的权力所在。同样，列宁赋予马克思“剥夺剥夺者”的号召以最字面的意义，敦促群众“抢回被抢走的东西”（
）。但这并不违反马克思关于历史逻辑的观点，因为武装强制始终是那一逻辑的组成部分。于是，十月为党在其建设社会主义的所有阶段继续使用强制手段开创了先例。
en: This so-called October Revolution was an “armed insurrection” carried out by the Party using the apparatus of the Petrograd Soviet,

Lenin insisted that the transfer of power take this militarized form rather than the political form of a vote by the forthcoming All-Russian Congress of Soviets, the course favored by his more pragmatic colleagues Grigorii Zinoviev and Lev Kamenev. And he did so because for him, as for Marx, the class struggle was literally class warfare, necessarily involving physical violence. No other method could adequately demonstrate where the real power lay. In the same manner, Lenin gave the most literal meaning to Marx’s call to “expropriate the expropriators” by urging the masses to “steal the stolen” (

). But this was no violation of Marx’s view of the logic of history, for armed coercion was always integral to that logic. And so, October set the precedent for the continuing use of coercion by the Party through all the stages of its construction of socialism.

zh: 列宁在芬兰的藏身之处，在科尔尼洛夫事件之后就开始施压要求举行这样的起义；到10月10日，他已说服中央委员会以10票对2票通过“原则上”采取这一行动。但组织起义的任务落到了列昂·托洛茨基身上。为了让党的政变显得更具无产阶级合法性，他推迟了起义，使之与即将召开的全国苏维埃代表大会同时举行——尽管列宁明确下令反对。托洛茨基还在苏维埃内部策划建立了一个军事革命委员会，这个委员会实际上由布尔什维克主导，负责执行对首都的实际接管。
en: Lenin, from his refuge in Finland, had initiated pressure for such an insurrection in the wake of the Kornilov affair, and by October 10 he had persuaded the Central Committee to vote 10 to 2 for such an action “in principle.” But the task of organizing the insurrection fell to Leon Trotsky, who, in order to give the Party coup an appearance of greater proletarian legitimacy, delayed it so that it would coincide with the forthcoming national Congress of Soviets—against Lenin’s express commands. Trotsky also engineered the creation within the Soviet of a Military Revolutionary Committee, which was in fact dominated by the Bolsheviks, to carry out the actual takeover of the capital.

zh: 换句话说，这场“革命”是一场少数人的军事行动，而不是像二月那样的大众事件。或者更准确地说，实际发生的事情，是军事革命委员会、一些波罗的海舰队水兵和少数工人赤卫队在10月24日至25日夜间接管首都神经中枢的一场业余警察行动。彼得格勒的“无产阶级”和该市卫戍部队绝大多数保持中立。由于没有任何力量为临时政府作战，布尔什维克几乎没有什么可推翻的。正如列宁本人所说，党“发现权力躺在街上，就干脆把它捡了起来”。
en: In other words, this “Revolution” was a minority military action, not a mass event like the one in February. Or, to be more precise, what occurred was an amateur police operation of the Military Revolutionary Committee, some sailors of the Baltic Fleet, and a handful of worker Red Guards to take over the nerve centers of the capital on the night of October 24-25. The Petrograd “proletariat” and the city’s military garrison remained overwhelmingly neutral. Because there were no forces to fight for the Provisional Government, the Bolsheviks had almost nothing to overthrow. As Lenin himself put it, the Party “found power lying in the streets and simply picked it up.”

zh: 于是，《四月提纲》中提出、此后被列宁一心一意推行的冒险策略，在十月的夺权中得到了回报。这位布尔什维克领袖此前不为大多数同胞所知，外界也完全不知道他，如今突然成了俄罗斯苏维埃共和国人民委员会主席，而这个政府事实上就是他的党在掌权。这个新政权立即发布了两项引人注目的法令：第一项是关于和平的法令，呼吁通过谈判结束战争，实际意味着俄国单方面退出冲突；第二项是关于土地的法令，将贵族和国家的地产社会化，实际意味着认可已经完成的农业革命。正如列宁在夺权之夜对托洛茨基所说：“让人头晕目眩。”
en: Thus the gambler’s strategy announced in the April Theses, and singlemindedly pursued by Lenin thereafter, paid off in the October seizure of power. The Bolshevik leader, hitherto unknown to most of his countrymen and quite unknown to the outside world, suddenly found himself the chairman of the Council of People’s Commissars of the Russian Soviet Republic, a government that was in fact his Party in power. This new power immediately issued two dramatic decrees: The first, “on Peace,” called for a negotiated end to the war, which in effect meant Russia’s unilateral withdrawal from the conflict; the second, “on Land,” socialized gentry and state properties, which in effect meant endorsing the already accomplished agrarian revolution. As Lenin put it to Trotsky on the night of the takeover: “It makes the head swim.”

zh: 这种对布尔什维克胜利的惊奇感，此后一直萦绕在史学中，并产生了另一个解释问题。这个问题源于两个事实：第一，布尔什维克党在很大程度上是列宁个人的创造；第二，他个人坚持武装起义，是导致十月政变的驱动力。但这些情况是否意味着，没有他，就不会有十月夺权，因而也不会有苏维埃政权？
en: This sense of wonder at the Bolshevik victory has lingered in the historiography ever since, where it has produced still another problem of interpretation. This problem arises from the facts, first, that the Bolshevik Party was largely Lenin’s personal creation, and second, that his personal insistence on armed insurrection was the driving force leading up to the October coup. But do these circumstances mean that without him there would have been no October takeover and hence no Soviet regime?

zh: 这种“伟人”史观的极端版本常常被提出。就连托洛茨基，尽管作为马克思主义者坚信客观社会逻辑在历史中的首要地位，也接近于认为列宁对布尔什维克的胜利不可或缺。但托洛茨基本来可以更谨慎一些，因为1917年的事件——从二月的第一号命令到十月左派社会革命党人的出现——表明，即便没有列宁，俄国左派中也有充足空间容纳一个主张“现在就革命”的极端主义政党。而且，在十月之前，列宁的党虽然是所有竞争的俄国政党中最等级森严的，但还不是后来那样完全听命于领袖、铁板一块的工具。
en: This extreme version of the “great man” theory of history has often been advanced. Even Trotsky, though committed as a Marxist to the primacy of an objective social logic in history, comes close to holding Lenin indispensable to Bolshevik victory. Yet Trotsky might well have been more cautious, for the events of 1917—from Order Number One in February to the emergence of the Left SRs in October—show that even without Lenin there was ample room on the Russian Left for an extremist party of “revolution now.” Moreover, before October it was the case that Lenin’s Party, though the most hierarchical of all the competing Russian parties, was not as yet the monolithic instrument commanded at will by its leader that it later became.

zh: 事实上，托洛茨基自己的历史角色就反驳了他赋予列宁的压倒性重要性；此外，它也凸显了1917年党的流动性。托洛茨基直到六月才放弃他自己那一派孟什维主义，加入布尔什维克行列；然而到十月，他已经在指挥布尔什维克的夺权。为了把党的接管与苏维埃代表大会协调起来，以增强政变的“无产阶级”外观，他甚至撤销了列宁急躁的指示。列宁虽然为政变提供了动力，却与政变的执行毫无关系，因为政变发生时他仍躲藏着。他真正更不可或缺的地方，是在此前十四年中作为党组织建筑师的角色；但即便在这个领域，到1917年也已有了许多小列宁，例如北方战线的伊万·斯米加（列宁实际上曾与他密谋，反对自己较为温和的中央委员会），这些人本可以推行同样的最大化政策。
en: Indeed, Trotsky’s own historical role belies the overriding importance he attributed to Lenin; in addition, it points up the fluidity of the Party in 1917. Trotsky abandoned his independent brand of Menshevism to enter the Bolshevik ranks only in June; yet by October he was directing the Bolshevik seizure of power. He even counter-manded Lenin’s impatient directives in order to coordinate the Party takeover with the Congress of Soviets, so as to enhance the coup’s “proletarian” appearance. Lenin, for all the impetus he gave to the coup, had nothing to do with carrying it out, since he was still in hiding when it came. Where he was more truly indispensable was in his role, over the previous fourteen years, as architect of the Party organization; yet even in this domain, by 1917, there were numerous little Lenins, such as Ivan Smilga on the Northern Front (with whom Lenin in fact conspired against his more moderate Central Committee), who could have pursued the same maximalist policies.

zh: 然而，更根本的是，《四月提纲》所阐述的最大化策略，只有在战争到1917年已在俄国造成的特殊社会环境中才行得通。因为那一年的核心事实是：一旦高度集权的俄罗斯帝国体系的轴心被拔掉，这个国家所有下属结构就开始瓦解。军队、工业经济、乡村社会结构、帝国的行政体系——无论是在大俄罗斯诸省，还是在边疆民族地区——都解体到如此地步，以至于到年底，这个国家已不再拥有任何运转中的、有组织的结构。结果是普遍的权力真空，国民生活一切方面的空位期。于是，到十月，俄罗斯帝国的残骸已可供争夺，谁有意志和组织能力，就任凭谁去接管。
en: More basically still, however, the maximalist strategy enunciated in the April Theses would work only in the exceptional social circumstances that the war had by 1917 created in Russia. For the central fact of that year is that once the linchpin of the hypercentralized Russian Imperial system was removed, all subordinate structures in the country began to unravel. The army, the industrial economy, the social structure of the countryside, and the administrative system of the Empire, both in the Great Russia provinces and among the border nationalities, all disintegrated to where, by the end of the year, the country no longer possessed any functioning, organized structures. The result was a generalized void of power, an interregnum in all aspects of national life. Thus, by October the wreckage of the Russian Empire was up for grabs, vulnerable to whatever force with the will and the organizational capacity to take it over.

zh: 国家解体的动力始于军队，并且全年首先由战争驱动。

临时政府的政策是与民主盟国一道把战争进行到胜利结束。苏维埃的政策则是只为“没有兼并和赔款的民主和平”而战。在第一号命令造成的破坏之后，纪律似乎一度恢复，四月成立的自由派—社会主义者联合政府于是采取折衷的战争政策，在六月发动了克伦斯基的“民主”攻势。这一自相矛盾的事业以溃败告终，再次破坏了军队纪律，并助长了七月事变中布尔什维克的攻势。而那一事件又导致科尔尼洛夫将军在八月试图扫除苏维埃，以恢复俄国的战斗力。但这一失败的努力最终使军队统帅部和军官团信誉扫地。因此，八月之后，军队干脆瓦解了，农民士兵长途跋涉回家，参加分配贵族土地。这样，从四月到七月再到八月的双重政权的一切政治危机，都直接由战争引起；到秋天，这些危机对军队的冲击已使国家的强制力量被摧毁。这种局面的名称就是无政府状态——尚未达到公开暴力的程度，但确实是政府缺位。
en: The dynamic of national disintegration began with the army and was driven throughout the year above all by the war.

The policy of the Provisional Government was to prosecute the war to a victorious conclusion at the side of its democratic allies. The policy of the Soviet was to fight only for a “democratic peace without annexations or indemnities.” Once discipline had seemingly been restored after the damage done by Order Number One, the liberal-socialist coalition government formed in April adopted a compromise war policy and so launched Kerenskii’s “democratic” offensive in June. This self-contradictory enterprise ended in a rout, undermined army discipline once again, and fueled the Bolshevik thrust of the July Days. And that event in turn led to General Kornilov’s attempt in August to restore Russia’s fighting capacity by sweeping away the soviets. But this failed effort definitively discredited the army command and officer corps. After August, therefore, the army simply melted away, with the peasant soldiers trekking home to participate in the partition of the gentry’s lands. Thus, all the political crises, of the dual power, from April to July to August, were directly caused by the war, and by autumn, the impact of these crises on the army was such that the coercive power of the state was destroyed. The name for such a situation is anarchy—not as yet of the overt and violent sort, but a genuine absence of government nonetheless.

zh: 正是这种无政府状态，才使1917年伟大的农业革命成为可能，即农民消灭贵族地产，实际上消灭作为阶级的俄国贵族。此前俄国所有的农民反抗都被镇压下去，因为前民主时代的军队始终保持完整。
en: This anarchy alone made possible the great agrarian revolution of 1917, that is, the liquidation by the peasantry of gentry land holdings, indeed, of the Russian gentry as a class. All peasant revolts in Russia had hitherto been suppressed because the predemocratic army had always remained intact.

zh: 没有穿军装的农民没有参加二月事变，但随着国家权威全年加速削弱，这些农民逐渐意识到，他们拥有全部土地的古老梦想终于触手可及。临时政府许诺在某个未来有利时刻召开立宪会议。这个机构当然有权处理土地问题，人人都预期它会满足农民的愿望。然而，这种几乎确定的满足并没有使农民的态度变得温和：它只是增加了他们的不耐烦。于是，在夏天，他们开始自行对贵族采取行动，并很快发现不会受到惩处；到秋天，一旦国家权威实际上消失，他们便大规模行动起来，没收乡村中的一切。这一行动又把士兵吸引回村庄参加大分配，从而加速了军队的解体。这场革命并不特别暴力或血腥：农民追求的是经济利益，而不是社会复仇。但这场革命异常彻底；到冬末，它已完全消灭了乡村延续一个世纪的领主—农民社会结构——这一结构曾与军队的军官—士兵等级制度密切相连。这场革命也消灭了斯托雷平改革的成果。
en: The peasant out of uniform had played no part in the February events, but as the weakening of state authority accelerated throughout the year, these peasants progressively realized that their age-old dream of possessing all the land was at last within grasp. The Provisional Government had promised a Constituent Assembly for some future, propitious moment. This body would of course be empowered to address the land question, and everyone expected it to accede to the peasants’ desires. Yet this near certainty of satisfaction did not moderate the attitude of the peasants: it simply increased their impatience. Thus during the summer they began to move against the gentry on their own and quickly discovered they could get away with this; by autumn, once state authority was virtually gone, they moved massively to expropriate everything in the countryside. This action in turn accelerated the disintegration of the army by drawing soldiers home to their villages to participate in the great partition. This revolution was not notably violent or murderous: The peasants were pursuing their economic interests, not social vengeance. But this revolution was extraordinarily thorough; by the end of the winter it had completely eliminated the century-old lord-peasant social structure of the countryside—a structure that had been intimately related to the officer-soldier hierarchy of the army. This revolution also liquidated the results of the Stolypin reform.

zh: 当这一切在帝国的大俄罗斯中心发生时，不安分的边疆民族也得以掌控自己的事务。大体而言，这分为两个阶段：到1917年夏，这些地区要求自治；到当年年底或次年初，随着布尔什维克掌权，它们开始主张独立。走在前头的是北方的芬兰大公国和基辅的乌克兰拉达（苏维埃）。（最持异议的民族波兰人，已处于德国占领之下。）到1918年初，波罗的海诸国和外高加索各民族同样躁动不安。于是，这个靠征服建立、靠武力维持的俄罗斯帝国，走上了创造它的军队同样的道路。
en: With all this transpiring in the Great Russian center of the Empire, the restive border nationalities were free to take control of their own affairs. For the most part, this occurred in two stages: by the summer of 1917 these regions were demanding autonomy, and by the end of the year or the beginning of the next, with the Bolsheviks in power, they were asserting their independence. Leading the way were the Grand Duchy of Finland in the north and the Ukrainian Rada (Soviet) in Kiev. (The most dissident nationality, the Poles, was already under German occupation.) By the beginning of 1918 the Baltic states and the Transcaucasian nations were equally restless. And so the Russian Empire, built through conquest and maintained by force, went the way of the army that had created it.

zh: 因此，在1917年过程中，旧俄国的一切结构——国家、军队、帝国、地方行政、经济，以及城市和乡村社会——同时分崩离析。这为本章开头提出的第二个问题提供了答案：在如此普遍崩溃之中，建立持久宪政民主没有任何现实机会。任何试图在这一革命进程完全展开之前加以干预的政府，都会信誉扫地。即便临时政府下定决心立即召开立宪会议、单方面让俄国退出战争、把土地交给农民——批评者后来认为它本应采取这些措施来阻止布尔什维主义——也很难产生预期结果。因为这些措施实际上类似于布尔什维克的政策。它们的效果将是革命性的、破坏性的，只会加深无政府状态，却不能给临时政府提供掌握局面的新强制手段——而那些手段对布尔什维克来说却是自然而然的。
en: Thus, in the course of 1917 all of old Russia’s structures—the state, the army, the Empire, the local administration, the economy, and both the urban and the rural societies—came apart simultaneously. This provides the answer to the second question posed at the beginning of the chapter: amidst such generalized collapse, there was no realistic chance of establishing a durable constitutional democracy. Any government that would have tried to intervene against this revolutionary process before its full unwinding would have been discredited. Even if the Provisional Government had found the resolve to immediately convene a Constituent Assembly, to unilaterally take Russia out of the war, and to give the land to the peasants—measures that critics later felt it should have adopted to stave off Bolshevism—this would hardly have had the desired result. For these measures were, in fact, similar to Bolshevik policy. They would have been revolutionary and disruptive in their effect, and they would have only deepened the anarchy without giving the Provisional Government the new coercive means to master it—means that came naturally to the Bolsheviks.

zh: 可悲的事实是，1917年解体的势头如此之大，以至于一旦它充分释放，要创造某种新秩序，只有威权的强制解决办法才可行。正如立宪民主党领袖米留可夫所说，到夏末，俄国面前的选择要么是科尔尼洛夫，要么是列宁。但由于科尔尼洛夫及他所象征的传统秩序力量没有实力，只有列宁和布尔什维克才能在社会风暴耗尽力量之后收拾残局，塑造一种新秩序。
en: The sad fact of the matter is that in 1917 the impetus for disintegration was such that, once it had played itself out, only an authoritarian, coercive solution was possible for creating some new type of order. As the Kadet leader Miliukov put the matter, by the end of the summer the alternatives for Russia were either Kornilov or Lenin. But since Kornilov and the forces of traditional order that he symbolized had no power, only Lenin and the Bolsheviks were in a position to pick up the pieces and to fashion a new type of order once the social storm had spent its force.

zh: 这种新秩序将是十月后宣布的“无产阶级专政”，作为从资本主义向社会主义过渡的工具。列宁在1917年夏写成的《国家与革命》中，依据马克思对巴黎公社的分析，把工人苏维埃的直接无产阶级民主解释为一种新的“公社国家”的实现。因此，苏维埃构成了未来专政和新的社会主义国家的基础。
这样，尽管俄国工人运动只有在国家普遍解体的进程中才可能获得“世界历史”意义，但这一更广泛进程的政治和意识形态意义，确实来自工人阶级行动，或者至少来自以工人阶级名义采取的行动。
en: This new type of order would be the “dictatorship of the proletariat” proclaimed after October as the vehicle for the transition from capitalism to socialism. Drawing on Marx’s analysis of the Paris Commune, during the summer of 1917 in

Lenin had interpreted the direct proletarian democracy of the workers’ soviets as the realization of a new “commune state.” As such, the soviets constituted the basis of the coming dictatorship and the new socialist state.

Thus, although it is only amidst a general process of national disintegration that the Russian workers’ movement could have acquired “world-historical” significance, this broader process indeed received its political and ideological meaning from working-class action or, at the least, from action in the name of the working class.

zh: 正是因为这个原因，无论东方还是西方，对俄国革命的解释都压倒性地关注工人阶级与布尔什维克党的关系。这个问题格外紧迫，因为苏维埃政权曾经能够主张的任何合法性——在它自己看来以及在外部世界看来——都取决于无产阶级与党的同体性，因而取决于十月的社会主义真实性。
en: It is for this reason that interpretation of the Russian Revolution, both in the East and in the West, has been overwhelmingly concerned with the working class in relation to the Bolshevik Party. This question is all the more urgent because whatever legitimacy the Soviet regime could once claim, in its own view and in that of the outside world, depended on the consubstantiality of the proletariat with the Party and, hence, on the socialist authenticity of October.

zh: 无产阶级还是党？
en: PROLETARIAT OR PARTY?

zh: 尽管显然有人不同意把布尔什维主义等同于工人阶级，但在1991年前的文献中，仍有一种主导倾向，把十月置于社会史的基础上，特别是把它说成劳动与资本之间“极化”或阶级斗争的产物。这种方法可以追溯到1917年本身，当时它第一次成为政治的主导话语。因为让我们回想，1905年俄国公众大体上并没有谈论“资产阶级”和“无产阶级”，而是用自由主义和反对专制的斗争的古典政治语言，来主张召开立宪会议。俄国政治词汇只是在立宪实验临近结束时才变成马克思主义的，而当“帝国主义战争”造成的紧张在1917年公开爆发时，这一过程达到了顶点。
en: Although there has obviously been dissent from the equating of Bolshevism with the working class, there has nonetheless been a dominant tendency in the pre-1991 literature to ground October in social history and, in particular, to make it the product of “polarization” or class struggle between labor and capital. This approach goes back to 1917 itself, when it first became the dominant discourse of politics. For let us recall that in 1905 the Russian public by and large had not spoken of the “bourgeoisie” and the “proletariat,” but instead had used the classical political language of liberalism and the struggle against autocracy to argue for a Constituent Assembly. The Russian political vocabulary became Marxist only towards the end of the constitutional experiment, and this process was brought to its culmination when the tensions generated by the “imperialist war” came out into the open in 1917.

zh: 这种词汇变化对1917年的事件产生了非常实际的影响。因为马克思主义总是把政治还原为社会学，从而模糊了公共生活中对权力的有目的运用。孟什维克尤其擅长这种还原论。他们特别论证说，布尔什维克之所以轻率地主张起义，是因为他们的支持来自刚脱离落后农民身份的工人，而具有真正无产阶级意识的熟练工人则被孟什维克自己吸引。这种把政治还原为社会基础的俄国马克思主义方式，自第二次世界大战以来极大地影响了西方关于1917年的写作。的确，1991年前西方修正主义写作的主要任务之一，就是修正孟什维克关于布尔什维克“基础”的旧看法，试图证明布尔什维克的工人同样具有成熟的无产阶级意识。
即便承认这一点属实，它对导致十月的政治过程以及那一事件的政治结果又有什么影响呢？
en: This change of vocabulary had a very real effect on events in 1917. For Marxism invariably reduces politics to sociology, thereby obfuscating the purposeful use of power in public life. The Mensheviks in particular were adept at such reductionism. They argued, notably, that the Bolsheviks were rashly insurrectionary because they drew their support from workers recently out of the backward peasantry, whereas skilled workers with a genuine proletarian consciousness gravitated towards the Mensheviks themselves. This Russian Marxist manner of reducing politics to social base has mightily influenced Western writing on 1917 since the Second World War. Indeed, one of the main tasks of pre-1991 Western revisionist writing was to revise the old Menshevik opinion of the Bolshevik “base” by seeking to demonstrate that the Bolsheviks’ workers, too, had a mature proletarian consciousness.
Even granting that this is true, what difference does it make to the political process leading to October, as well as to the political results of that event?

zh: 事实上，双重政权也出现在俄国的工厂里，正如它出现在军队、乡村和城市行政中一样。工业中的双重政权表现为工厂委员会，其职责是监督管理人员和工程技术人员。这些委员会的最低目标，是从厂主那里争得典型的工会让步。其中一项让步——四十小时工作周——实际上在六月通过罢工和其他形式的劳工压力获得了，而厂主有时以闭厂作为回应，虽然效果不大，却颇具威胁。在这种经典的劳工斗争中，工人得到了温和社会主义政党（孟什维克和社会革命党人）的积极支持。当然，这一切进一步扰乱了生产，而这场战争正是这些社会主义者现在所支持的。然而工厂委员会的最大目标更具破坏性；这个目标是“工人控制工业”，最初意味着工人监督资本，后来逐渐意味着工人接管工厂。简言之，1917年俄国工厂中确实存在阶级斗争。结果，猜疑和不信任弥漫于俄国工业，而工业正迅速陷入停顿。
en: And, in fact, dual power appeared in Russia’s factories just as it had in the army, the countryside, and the administration of the cities. Industrial dual power took the form of factory committees designed to oversee management and engineering personnel. These committees had the minimal goal of wresting classic trade union concessions from the factory owners. One such concession, the forty-hour workweek, was in fact obtained in June through strikes and other forms of labor pressure that at times were ineffectually yet threateningly answered by lockouts. In this classic type of labor struggle the workers were actively supported by the moderate (Menshevik and SR) socialist parties. And all of this, of course, further disrupted production for a war these same socialists now supported. Yet the maximal goal of the factory committees was even more disruptive; this goal was “workers’ control of industry,” which initially meant worker supervision of capital but in time came to mean worker takeover of the plants. In short, there was real class struggle in Russia’s factories in 1917. In consequence, distrust and suspicion pervaded Russian industry as it was rapidly grinding to a halt.

zh: 然而，这场社会革命的政治后果是含糊的。一方面，从四月到十月，工人的情绪激进化，越来越敌视“帝国主义”战争、“资本主义”临时政府，以及支持战争并与“资产阶级”结盟的“叛卖”温和社会主义政党。另一方面，整个1917年，工人的积极性和战斗精神却在下降；这些在二月事变期间达到顶峰，当时工人承担了真正的风险，并付出了1700人伤亡的代价。四月危机和七月事变引起了规模较小、但仍可观的工人街头动员。但民众对科尔尼洛夫事件的反应很微弱，而十月根本不是群众事件，而是由少数布尔什维克党干部和附属军事单位执行的一次行动。因此，到十月，1917年的革命势头正在减弱，工人阶级同俄国社会其他组成部分一样，作为一个群体正在解体，在不断求生的斗争中疲惫不堪。
en: The political consequences of this social revolution, however, were ambiguous. On one hand, from April to October the mood of the workers radicalized and became increasingly hostile to the “imperialist” war, the “capitalist” Provisional Government, and the “traitorous” moderate socialist parties that supported the war and the coalition with the “bourgeoisie.” On the other hand, worker activism and militancy declined throughout 1917; these had reached their peak during the February Days, when the workers took real risks and payed with seventeen hundred casualties. The April crisis and the July Days produced a lesser though still respectable mobilization of workers in the streets. But popular reaction to the Kornilov incident was meager, and October was not a mass affair at all but an operation carried out by a small number of Bolshevik Party cadres and affiliated military units. Thus by October the revolutionary momentum of 1917 was winding down as the working class, along with the other components of Russian society, was disintegrating as a group and succumbing to weariness amidst a constant struggle to survive.

zh: 那么，这个工人阶级究竟是如何在十月掌权的？事实上，它当然没有掌权；掌权的是一个政治和意识形态组织，即布尔什维克党。这引出两个问题：一个是关于这个党的性质及其与工人关系的直接经验问题；另一个是关于任何情况下“社会基础”与政治权力关系的一般理论问题。
en: How, then, did this working class come to power in October? In fact, of course, it did not come to power; what came to power was a political and ideological organization, the Bolshevik Party. This raises two questions: the immediate empirical question of the nature of this Party and its relationship to the workers; and the general theoretical question of the relationship of “social base” to political power in any situation.

zh: 先谈第一个问题，我们必须回到列宁1902年在《怎么办？》中的号召：建立一个由专职革命者组成的“新型政党”。他认为这样的团体是必要的，部分原因是1905年前俄国一切政治生活都必须在非法和秘密的条件下进行。但他的首要理由是，工人的“自发工联主义”必须由“先锋”党的“自觉”和“科学”革命理论来启发。换句话说，布尔什维克党是引领人类走向社会主义革命的历史逻辑的载体——或者用实际的话说，党是革命知识分子的替身。至于实际工人，他们只有在为革命工作、而不是为短期经济利益工作时，才参与党的生活。如果工人落入后一种“修正主义”陷阱，他们就不再是真正的无产者，而成为“小资产阶级”的一部分，其天然代言人就是“叛卖”的孟什维克或“叛徒”德国社会民主党人。因为社会上基本上只有两个阶级、两种世界观，即无产阶级和资产阶级；任何政治行动者，无论其实际阶级属性如何，只要没有科学的革命意识，就自动是
，是敌人。因此，列宁主义政党代表的是一个形而上学的、而非经验的无产阶级；这种意识形态“意识”对现实生活的优先性，就是列宁对阶级斗争的理解，也是他全部政治的驱动力。
en: To begin with the first question, we must return to Lenin’s call, in 1902 in

, for “a party of a new type,” composed of full-time revolutionaries, Such a body he deemed necessary in part because of the conditions of illegality and clandestinity that weighed on all political life in Russia before 1905. But his paramount reason was that the “spontaneous trade unionism” of the workers had to be informed by the “conscious” and “scientific” revolutionary theory of the “vanguard” party. In other words, the Bolshevik Party was the vehicle for the logic of history that would lead mankind to the socialist revolution—or in practical terms the Party was a surrogate for the revolutionary intelligentsia. As for the actual workers, they participated in the Party’s life only insofar as they worked for revolution and not for short-term economic gains. If the workers fell into the latter “revisionist” trap, they ceased being authentic proletarians and became part of the “petty bourgeoisie,” whose natural spokesmen were the “traitorous” Mensheviks or the “renegade” German SDs. For there existed basically only two classes with two worldviews in society, the proletariat and the bourgeoisie; if any political actor, whatever his de facto class, did not have a scientific revolutionary consciousness, he was automatically a

and an enemy. The Leninist Party thus represented a metaphysical, not an empirical, proletariat, and this primacy of ideological “consciousness” over real life was Lenin’s understanding of the class struggle and the driving force of all his politics.

zh: 1917年10月夺取政权的，正是这个由意识形态定义的政治组织，而不是单纯经验意义上的无产阶级。然而，为了做到这一点，党至少在跃上权力宝座所需的这段时间里，绝对需要真实工人阶级的支持。党的领袖们也确实需要相信党与真实工人是一体的，正如许多工人也真诚地相信同样的事情。正是基于这种误解，列宁和党的领导层在1917年把他们精英主导的活动转变为一个暂时性的群众组织。
en: It is this ideologically defined political organization, and not the mere empirical proletariat, that seized power in October 1917. In order to do this, however, the Party had an absolute need of real working-class support for at least as long as it took to vault into power. Its leaders also genuinely needed to believe that the Party and the real workers were in fact one, just as numerous workers sincerely believed the same thing. And it is on the basis of this misunderstanding that Lenin and the Party leadership in 1917 transformed their elite operation into a temporary mass organization.

zh: 尽管有莫斯科十二月起义的骚动，布尔什维克在1905年的事件中并未扮演重要角色；事实上，列宁甚至没有及时回到俄国参加革命。布尔什维克只是在1912年之后才开始获得可观的——尽管远非群众性的——追随者；到1914年夏的罢工时，他们已在工人中领先孟什维克。但这一切都被1914年8月战争爆发后的爱国浪潮冲垮了。因此，1917年二月之后，布尔什维克——以及其他革命政党——不得不重新建立自己的群众基础。然而到当年夏末，布尔什维克在城市和北方前线又再次领先于孟什维克和社会革命党人。但鉴于工人阶级政治参与的流动性和短暂时间跨度，断言无产阶级对任何一个党组织有深刻而持久的承诺，是牵强的。
en: The Bolsheviks had played no significant role in the events of 1905, despite the flurry of the Moscow December insurrection; in fact, Lenin did not even return to Russia in time for the Revolution. The Bolsheviks began to acquire a significant, though hardly a mass, following only after 1912; by the time of the strikes in the summer of 1914, they had pulled ahead of the Mensheviks among the workers. But all this was dashed by the patriotic wave that followed the out break of war in August. Thus the Bolsheviks—and the other revolutionary parties as well—had to build their popular base all over again after February 1917. By the late summer of that year, however, the Bolsheviks had again pulled ahead of the Mensheviks and the SRs in the cities and the northern part of the front. But given the fluid nature and the short time span of working-class political involvement, it is far-fetched to argue that the proletariat had any deep and enduring commitment to any one party organization.

zh: 尽管如此，在四月到十月之间，布尔什维克党成了更激进工人的暂时首选。根据党当时对自身力量的估计，1917年初党员为23600人，尽管其中大多数不得已只能秘密参加为数不多的党务活动。
到1918年1月，党员约为115000人，很可能更多；约60%的党员被归为工人，32%是“白领”雇员或小知识分子。列宁的党第一次不再是本质上由职业革命者组成的组织，而成为一个主要由工人组成的团体。
en: Nonetheless, between April and October the Bolshevik Party became the provisional preference of the more radicalized workers. According to the Party’s own estimation of its strength at the time, its membership was 23,600 at the beginning of 1917, although most of these of necessity participated clandestinely in what little Party activity there was.

By January 1918 membership was around 115,000, and quite possibly more; some 60 percent of the members were classified as workers, while 32 percent were “white-collar” employees or petty intelligentsia. For the first time, Lenin’s Party ceased being essentially an organization of professional revolutionaries and became a body composed predominantly of workers.

zh: 此外，这个新党并不是一支可由领导层任意调动的纪律严明的军队。其基层，尤其是在彼得格勒，比中央委员会更激进、更不耐烦，对列宁及其同事施加了相当大的压力；决策在很大程度上通过包含辩论和投票的过程作出。在组织上，如前所述，党具有社会民主党的经典结构：中央委员会由代表大会选举产生，代表大会由地方委员会选举产生。正是1917年布尔什维主义的这些特征，被称为“民主的”。
但这种民主只存在于一个阶级的成员即工人之中，也只存在于党内的政治生活之中。而在弥漫于这个组织的列宁主义意识形态中，社会其余部分和一切竞争性政治组织——甚至其他社会主义政党——都被视为阶级敌人，视为“资产阶级”或“小资产阶级”，因此一旦真正的无产阶级政党掌权，就必须消灭它们。这样，1917年那个多少具有“群众性”的布尔什维克党，从来不是愿意与其他群体分享权力或轮替掌权的意义上的民主政党。
en: This new Party, moreover, was not a disciplined army to be maneuvered at will by the leadership. The base, especially in Petrograd, was more radical and impatient than the Central Committee and exerted considerable pressure on Lenin and his colleagues; decisions were largely made through a process that involved debates and votes. Organizationally, as already noted, the Party had the classic structure of a Social Democratic Party, with a Central Committee chosen by a Congress elected by local committees. It is these characteristics of 1917 Bolshevism that have been called “democratic.”

But this democracy existed only for members of one class, the workers, and only for politics within the Party. And in the Leninist ideology that pervaded this organization, the rest of society and all rival political organizations—even the other socialist parties—were regarded as class enemies, as “bourgeois” or “petty-bourgeois,” who therefore would have to be eliminated once the true party of the proletariat came to power. Thus, the more or less “mass” Bolshevik Party of 1917 was never democratic in the sense of being willing to share power, or to alternate in power, with other groups.

zh: 这一情况为理解十月颠覆提供了钥匙。从《四月提纲》到秋天，列宁的组织通过不断鼓动结束双重政权、支持以阶级为基础的苏维埃来建立影响。布尔什维克的口头禅是“面包、和平、土地，全部政权归苏维埃”。这个纲领是不负责任的、煽动性的，因为正如列宁的社会主义对手不断指出的，由苏维埃夺取政权事实上并不能解决面包、和平或土地问题。但作为革命政治，这个纲领非常合理，因为它动员了因日益绝望的局势而愤怒的工人和士兵，目的是为“劳动者”夺取政权。
en: This circumstance provides the key to understanding the October overturn. From the April Theses on into the autumn, Lenin’s organization built its influence through a drumbeat of agitation for the end of dual power in favor of the class-based soviets. The Bolsheviks’ refrain was “bread, peace, land, all power to the soviets.” This program was irresponsible and demagogic in the sense that the seizure of power by the soviets would not in fact solve the problems of bread, peace, or land, as Lenin’s socialist adversaries constantly pointed out. But this program made great sense as revolutionary politics because it mobilized workers and soldiers angry with an increasingly desperate situation with the purpose of seizing power for the “toilers.”

zh: 但正如我们所见，劳动者并没有直接夺取政权。
党替他们夺取了政权，这一点通过与二月的对比表现得最清楚。十月没有像二月那样数十万罢工者连续五天在街头面对真正危险，也没有那次事件中1700人的伤亡。十月的街头没有工人，受害者人数约为十几人。因此，这些“震撼世界的十天”，实际上是一场政变；而为否认这一明显事实所投入的巨大努力，是一个经典案例：过分抗辩反而间接承认了有东西要隐瞒。
的确，直到1920年代中期，布尔什维克自己都把十月称为
，即“颠覆”或政变。尽管如此，这场政变确实以空前的、具有世界历史意义的方式震撼了世界；因为尽管经验意义上的无产阶级大体上缺席了伟大的十月，形而上学意义上的无产阶级却被弹射上台，而这个政治—意识形态实体将被证明，比全世界所有真实工人的联合都更具革命性。
en: But, as we have seen, the toilers did not seize power directly.

That the Party did it for them is best brought out by the contrast with February. In October there was nothing like the hundreds of thousands of strikers who had faced real danger in the streets for five days in February, nor was there anything like the seventeen hundred casualties of that event. In October the streets were empty of workers, and the number of victims was around a dozen. These “ten days that shook the world,” therefore, were in reality a coup d’état, and the prodigious efforts deployed to deny this obvious fact are a classic case where protesting too much is an indirect admission of something to hide.
Indeed, until the mid-1920s the Bolsheviks themselves called October a

that is, an “overturn” or coup. Nonetheless, this coup did in fact shake the world in an unprecedented and world-historical manner; for, although the empirical proletariat largely sat out Great October, the metaphysical proletariat was catapulted into power, and this political-ideological entity would prove to be far more revolutionary than all the real workers of the world united.

zh: 当然，彼得格勒的事件并不等于十月革命的全部：例如在莫斯科，就有一场真正的斗争和更多伤亡。在随后的日子里，布尔什维克和左派社会革命党人领导的地方苏维埃在全国大部分地区从
手中夺取了控制权。尽管这算不上苏联史学曾经所说的布尔什维克政权的“凯旋进军”，但作为对彼得格勒政变的响应，确实发生了一场全国性的苏维埃革命。
en: To be sure, the events in Petrograd were not the whole of the October Revolution: in Moscow, for example, there was a genuine struggle and a greater number of victims. And in the days that followed, local soviets under Bolshevik and Left-SR leadership took control from the

throughout much of the country. Although this hardly amounted to the “triumphal march” of Bolshevik power of which Soviet historiography once spoke, there was in fact a national revolution of soviets in answer to the Petrograd coup.

zh: 然而，只有把它与1917—1918年冬天的农民暴动结合起来看，十月革命才可被视为全国性的；那场暴动消灭了乡村的贵族土地占有制，使农民（暂时）成为自己的主人。这场农业革命当然不是由布尔什维克指挥或控制的，尽管他们的鼓动者提倡农民夺取贵族土地。
但在政治上从这场农民暴动中获益最大的正是布尔什维克，他们把它收编进一个统一的伟大十月的神话。
en: The October Revolution may be considered national, however, only in conjunction with the peasant jacquerie of the winter of 1917-1918 which liquidated gentry landholding in the countryside and made the peasants (temporarily) their own masters. This agrarian revolution was, of course, neither commanded nor controlled by the Bolsheviks, although their agitators advocated seizure of gentry lands by the peasants.
Yet it was the Bolsheviks who profited most from the jacquerie politically, incorporating it into the myth of a single Great October.

zh: 这次没收得到了社会革命党左翼的协助。他们于十月从社会革命党主流中分裂出来，支持布尔什维克夺权，因为他们认为这意味着苏维埃政权。于是列宁得以宣称，他的苏维埃政府代表了“工人和农民的革命联盟”。这也正是他10月25日土地法令的真正含义：按照社会革命党传统的纲领把土地社会化。然而事实上，这项法令只是为布尔什维克的目的占用了一个既成事实，因为政府在乡村无力决定事件的进程。正如列宁当时所说，布尔什维克的政策只是“放开缰绳，让农民这匹老马自行前行”。
en: This confiscation was facilitated by the left wing of the SRs, who seceded from the main SR party in October to support the Bolshevik seizure of power because they thought it meant soviet power. Thus Lenin was able to claim that his Soviet government represented a “revolutionary alliance of workers and peasants.” And this was the real meaning of his Decree on Land of October 25, socializing the land in accordance with the traditional SR program. In fact, however, the decree simply appropriated a fait accompli for Bolshevik purposes, since the government could do nothing to determine the course of events in the countryside. As Lenin put it at the time, Bolshevik policy was simply “to give the peasant nag its head.”

zh: 列宁与农民“革命联盟”的政策，以及他对社会革命党土地纲领的占用，常常被引用来——尤其是被孟什维克和社会革命党人引用来——证明十月不是一场真正的马克思主义革命，而是对1870年代俄国民粹主义传统的倒退。这里面确实有些道理：列宁确实把车尔尼雪夫斯基和民粹派的遗产与马克思主义融合在一起。但占上风的是马克思主义；因为列宁从未打算让土地按照社会革命党的真正政策保持“社会化”，即留在农民自己手中。因此，1918年2月，他的政府将所有土地国有化，把法定所有权交到国家手中。虽然布尔什维克暂时无法实施这项措施，但它至少暴露了他们的真实目标。
en: Lenin’s policy of “revolutionary alliance” with the peasantry and his appropriation of the SR land program have often been cited—especially by Mensheviks and SRs—as proof that October was not a proper Marxist revolution but a throwback to the Russian Populist tradition of the 1870s. There is indeed some truth in this: Lenin did fuse the heritage of Chernyshevskii and the Populists with Marxism. But it was the Marxism that came out on top; for Lenin never intended that the land would remain “socialized,” that is, in the peasants’ own hands, in accordance with the real SR policy. Accordingly, in February 1918 his government nationalized all land and put legal title to it in the hands of the state. Although for the time being the Bolsheviks could not implement this measure, it did at least reveal their true aims.

zh: 而且，列宁对民粹主义的有限借用，在马克思主义本身中有充分依据。创始人本人在1882年致民粹派领袖维拉·查苏利奇的信中，曾认可把俄国的农民革命与西方的无产阶级革命结合起来（这份文件被普列汉诺夫和恩格斯合谋压下，以免使初生的俄国马克思主义运动感到震惊）。列宁在1917年自认为遵循的正是这样一种策略。更早的1851年，马克思曾论证，他自己落后的德国可以把资产阶级革命和无产阶级革命压缩在一起，并搭上法国社会主义剧变的便车；这一剧本稍向东移，就是列宁在1917年自认为正在实施的东西。
en: Moreover, there is good Marxist authority for Lenin’s limited borrowings from Populism. The founder himself, in a letter to the Populist leader Vera Zasulich in 1882, had approved of combining a peasant revolution in Russia with a proletarian revolution in the West (a document Plekhanov and Engels conspired to suppress lest it scandalize the nascent Russian Marxist movement). And it is just such a strategy Lenin thought he was following in 1917. Earlier still, in 1851, Marx had argued that his own backward Germany could telescope the bourgeois and proletarian revolutions and ride piggyback on a socialist upheaval in France; this scenario, shifted a bit to the east, is what Lenin also thought he was carrying out in 1917.

zh: 然而，真正反对对列宁的正统性吹毛求疵的理由在于：这个问题只对那些认为马克思主义的本质在于其从封建主义到资本主义再到社会主义的刻板相继公式的人，才成其为问题。但马克思主义的本质——让我们回想——在于其深层结构：依靠最受剥夺的阶级的异化，作为革命的造物主；而农民阶级作为普遍阶级的初级一翼，相当合乎逻辑地嵌入了这个模具。列宁像马克思一样（后来也像毛泽东一样），会在发现革命火种的地方取火，并相应调整其理论的形式化教条。正如我们所见，列宁的帝国主义理论也作了类似的调整，使俄国成为“资本主义链条中最薄弱的一环”。说到底，马克思主义的要旨是改变世界，而不仅仅是理解世界。
en: The real objection to caviling about Lenin’s orthodoxy, however, is that this is an issue only for those who hold that the essence of Marxism lies in its formal tenets of lockstep succession from feudalism to capitalism to socialism. But the essence of Marxism—let us recall—lies in its deep structure of reliance on the alienation of the most deprived classes as the demiurge of revolution; and the peasantry fitted quite logically into this mold as the junior wing of the universal class. Lenin, like Marx (and later like Mao), would take the fire of revolution where he found it, and adjust the formal tenets of his theory accordingly. A similar adjustment, as we have seen, was achieved by Lenin’s theory of imperialism, which made Russia the “weakest link in the capitalist chain.” What Marxism is all about, after all, is changing the world, not just understanding it.

zh: 因此，正是多亏了农民，世界上第一场马克思主义革命才发生在唯一可能发生它的欧洲国家——俄国。而这场革命又以俄国条件下唯一可能的方式发生——作为工人
农民的运动。于是，所有劳动者在一个综合体中联合起来，其标志就是绣在国际主义红旗上的锤子和镰刀。正如新苏维埃国歌《国际歌》所唱，“

zh: ”（大地上受苦受难的人们、饥饿的奴隶），从未有谁如此真切地表现为来自下层的普遍阶级。
en: Thus, it was thanks to the peasantry that the world’s first Marxist revolution occurred in the only European country it could—Russia. And this revolution occurred in the only way it could under Russian conditions—as a movement of workers
peasants. So all of the toilers were brought together in a synthesis under the sign of the hammer and sickle emblazoned on the internationalist red flag. Never before had “
