en: ” as the new Soviet anthem, the “Internationale,” put it, so truly appeared to be the universal class from below.

zh: 不过，作为进步阶级和技术阶级的工人，仍必须保持这场运动的先锋地位，而他们所谓的彼得格勒“武装起义”，必须成为红色十月世界历史性转变的关键事件。当然，真实工人对这场形而上学事件绝对必要。诚然，这些工人响应党的时间很短，远不足以像西欧的工会之于社会主义政党那样构成党的“社会基础”。尽管如此，这些工人仍是党借以弹射上台的不可或缺的跳板。
en: Still, the workers, as the progressive and technological class, had to remain the vanguard of this movement, and their alleged “armed insurrection” in Petrograd had to be the pivotal event of the world-historical transformation of Red October. And, of course, the real workers were absolutely necessary to this metaphysical event. To be sure, these workers had hardly been responsive to the Party long enough to constitute its “social base” the way trade unions, say, have been the base of socialist parties in Western Europe. Nonetheless, these workers were the indispensable springboard from which the party catapulted to power.

zh: 但仅凭这块跳板还不够：俄国国家体系的其余部分——国家结构、军队、乡村秩序——也必须处于终末危机之中。因此总体而言，十月代表的是有史以来最大的军事哗变、历史上最大的农民暴动，与一个人工制造出来的巴黎公社仿制品三者的结合。
en: But this springboard alone would not have been enough: The rest of the Russian national system—the state structures, the army, the rural order—had to be in terminal crisis as well. Thus overall, October represents a conjunction of the greatest military mutiny of all time, and the greatest peasant jacquerie in history, with a simulacrum, artificially engineered, of the Paris Commune.

zh: 事实上，把这个“小公社”与1871年公社或1848年巴黎六月起义相比——对所有马克思主义者来说，这两者是无产阶级革命应有的样板——是很不恰当的。因为后两者都是真正具有英雄气概的城市（如果算不上真正“无产阶级”的）起义。事实上，人们不禁想借用马克思那句名言——历史总是重演，第一次是悲剧，第二次是闹剧——来形容红色十月，而列宁在彼得格勒的“起义”正属于后一种类型。
en: In reality, the comparison of this communette with the Commune of 1871 or with the Paris June Days of 1848—the two models, for all Marxists, of what a proletarian revolution should be like—is quite abusive. For these latter two events were genuine urban (if not actually “proletarian”) insurrections of heroic proportions. In fact, one is tempted to adapt Marx’s
that history always repeats itself—first as tragedy, then as farce—to Red October, with Lenin’s Petrograd “insurrection” very much in the latter genre.

zh: 在十月三要素——哗变、农民暴动、小公社——中，抽掉前两个要素中的任何一个，“彼得格勒公社”无论是在君主制还是共和制下，都一定会像它的巴黎前辈被法国农村镇压那样，被农民士兵镇压。抽掉第一次世界大战，就既不会有哗变，也不会有它在普遍农民暴动中的社会延伸。正是所有这些因素共同作用，而不是某种无产阶级—资产阶级极化，构成了十月真正的社会史。
en: Take away either of the first two elements of the October triad of mutiny-jacquerie-communette, and the “Petrograd Commune”—whether occurring under a monarchy or a republic—would have been crushed by the peasant soldier just as surely as was its Parisian predecessor by rural France. Take away the First World War, and there would have been neither the mutiny nor its social prolongation in the universal jacquerie. It is all these factors working together, not some proletarian-bourgeois polarization, that constitutes the real social history of October.

zh: 从这个视角，我们找到了本章开头提出的第三个问题的答案，即俄国国内社会进程与战争冲击在产生十月的过程中各自扮演了什么角色。答案显然是，这两个因素共同起作用，尽管不是把后者简单叠加到前者之上。旧俄国那个残酷等级化的社会中并不缺乏社会紧张，而战争的苦难把这些紧张加剧到杀戮性的强度。因此最终发生的社会极化远比1905—1906年更具爆炸性，而这一情况又延续到随后那场甚至更为异常残酷的内战。此外，战争摧毁了本可以约束这种极化的国家权力制度性限制。
en: It is in this perspective that we find the answer to the third question posed at the beginning of this chapter, namely, what were the respective roles of Russia’s internal social processes and the impact of the war in producing October? The answer, obviously, is that the two factors acted in combination, though not through any simple addition of the latter to the former. Although there was no lack of social tension in the brutally hierarchical society that was old Russia, these tensions were aggravated to murderous intensity by the sufferings of the war. Thus the social polarization that finally occurred was far more explosive than that of 1905-1906, a circumstance that continued into the even more exceptionally brutal Civil War that ensued. Moreover, the war destroyed the institutional restraints of state power that might have held this polarization in check.

zh: 鉴于这些沉重的“偶然性”，把十月主要视为俄国社会进程逻辑的结果是牵强的：有些时候，偶然性本身就是结构，俄国革命就是其中一例。而接受党对自身的定义——一个无产阶级组织——就更加牵强。这两个命题都是神话。
en: In view of such weighty “contingencies,” it is far-fetched to view October primarily as the outcome of the logic of Russia’s social processes: There are times when contingency itself is structure, and the role of the Russian Revolution is one of these. And it is even more far-fetched to accept the Party’s definition of itself as a proletarian organization. Both of these propositions are myths.

zh: 然而，十月的神话对于布尔什维克当时的胆量、对于他们掌权后自上而下的无情革命行动，以及对于他们的国际成功，都是不可或缺的。这些神话也有足够的经验支撑，足以在参与其中的行动者眼中以及此后的大部分史学中显得像科学事实一样可信。但党与无产阶级的这种重叠被证明是短暂的。到1918年初，我们将会看到，无产阶级已开始作为一个有凝聚力的社会群体溶解；内战后，党已根深蒂固，不再需要任何社会基础来维持权力。因此，那个在研究十月时让人反复纠缠的布尔什维主义社会史问题，随着我们进入苏维埃时代本身，很快就变得无足轻重。
en: Nevertheless, the October myths were indispensable to the Bolsheviks’ daring at the time and to their ruthless revolutionary action from above once they were in power—as well as to their international success. And these myths had sufficient empirical underpinning to appear credible as scientific facts, both to the actors involved and in much of the historiography since. Yet this overlap of Party and proletariat proved transitory. By early 1918, as we will see, the proletariat had begun to dissolve as a cohesive social group; and after the Civil War the Party was so firmly entrenched that it required no social base of any kind to remain in power. Thus the issue of the social history of Bolshevism, so obsessive for October, quickly fades into insignificance as we move into the Soviet era itself.

zh: 此外，即便在1917年末至1918年初党与工人重叠最大的时候，这种重叠也在很大程度上基于一种误解。诚然，工人在十月想要一个苏维埃政府，但要的是一个由所有社会主义政党组成的联合政府。事实上，一些布尔什维克领导人，特别是加米涅夫和季诺维也夫，也想要同样的东西，这就是他们对十月态度谨慎、列宁也总是多少不信任他们的原因。而在1918年初的几个月里，列宁确实机会主义地接受了与左派社会革命党人的联合。但从一开始，党内多数领导人，尤其是十月的主要设计师列宁和托洛茨基，只打算建立一个一党制的布尔什维克政权，直到实现社会主义为止。在他们看来，而且在此后苏维埃国家看来，十月代表着民主合法性从人民到党的一次性、永久性转移，无需任何“资产阶级”式的授权更新。因此，米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫直到最后都总是谈论“十月作出的社会主义选择”。但完全无端的是，假定俄国工人在支持或默许十月颠覆时，曾打算对党作出任何这种确定性的承诺。
en: Moreover, even in late 1917-early 1918, when the overlap between Party and workers was greatest, it was based largely on a misunderstanding. To be sure, in October the workers wanted a government of soviets, but one that would be a coalition of all of the socialist parties. Indeed, a number of Bolshevik leaders, notably Kamenev and Zinoviev, wanted the same thing, which is why they had been reticent about October and why Lenin always somewhat distrusted them. And, for a few months in early 1918, Lenin did opportunistically accept a coalition with the Left SRs. But from the beginning, the majority of the Party leadership, and certainly the great architects of October, Lenin and Trotsky, intended only a one-party Bolshevik regime for as long as it would take to reach socialism. In their view, and in that of the Soviet state ever after, October represented a once-and-forever transmission of democratic legitimacy from people to Party, with no need for any “bourgeois” renewal of mandate. Thus Mikhail Gorbachev, until the very end, always spoke of “the socialist choice made in October.” But it is quite gratuitous to assume that the workers of Russia intended any such definitive commitment to the Party when they endorsed, or acquiesced in, the October overturn.

zh: 我们确实知道，工人在十月想要的是“工人控制工业”和剥夺“

”，他们试图通过这些措施确保对自己社会环境的直接控制。但这与完整社会主义远不是一回事，尽管工人确实非常笼统地使用了“社会主义”一词。而且，这种模糊的社会主义可以通过工人对由所有三个社会主义政党组成的联合苏维埃政府的政治偏好来保障。但布尔什维克的真正目标，是完整意义上的“建设社会主义”，而不是某种无政府工团主义的“工人控制”。建设社会主义究竟意味着什么，就连党的领导层在1917年也不清楚；但无论需要什么，显然都不取决于工人的意志或选择。值得注意的是，10月25日并没有一项戏剧性的“工人监督法令”来伴随“土地法令”，因为在列宁主义看来，党
无产阶级。直到一个月后，工人控制才被写入法律。
en: What we do know the workers wanted in October was “workers’ control of industry” and the dispossession of the “

” measures by which they sought to secure direct control over their social environment. But this is hardly the same as integral socialism, even though the workers did use the term “socialism” in a very general fashion. This vague socialism, moreover, could be secured by the workers’ political preference for a coalition soviet government of all three socialist parties. But “building socialism” in the integral sense, not some anarcho-syndicalist “workers’ control,” was the true aim of the Bolsheviks. Just what, precisely, the building of socialism entailed, not even the Party leadership knew in 1917; but whatever was required clearly did not depend on the will or choice of the workers. zh: 但十月无产阶级性质的问题，比那一事件的政治和社会偶然性更为深刻。提出这个问题本身，就预设了无产阶级革命的存在。然而，即便最粗略地考察欧洲历史也会表明：如果十月不是真货，那么任何地方、任何时候都从未有过无产阶级革命。资产阶级革命或许也可以这样说。这类事件唯一勉强可信的例子是1789年的法国；的确，法国案例为整个观念提供了模型。在其他任何地方——无论是在英国、德国还是美国——资产阶级都不需要一场政治革命来掌权（如果“资产阶级掌权”确实恰当地描述了任何地方的现代宪政安排的话）；法国案例也没有向我们展示最具活力的工业资产阶级。此外，资产阶级革命和无产阶级革命都代表着从单一案例进行概括的古怪做法。然而，在这种分析模式中，这些明显的经验考虑是次要的；因为在讨论从资产阶级革命到无产阶级革命的进程时，我们面对的不是社会学，而是末世论。
en: But the question of the proletarian nature of October goes deeper than the political and social contingencies of that event. To pose the question at all presupposes the existence of proletarian revolutions. Yet even the most cursory examination of European history shows that if October is not the genuine article, then there never has been a proletarian revolution, anywhere, anytime. The same might also be said of bourgeois revolutions. The only halfway plausible example of such an event is France in 1789; indeed, the French case furnished the model for the whole idea. Nowhere else—neither in England nor in Germany nor in the United States—did the bourgeoisie require a political revolution to come to power (if indeed “bourgeoisie in power” appropriately describes modern constitutional arrangements anywhere); nor does the French case offer us the industrial bourgeoisie at its most dynamic. Moreover, both the bourgeois revolution and the proletarian revolution represent the oddity of generalizations from a single case. Yet these obvious empirical considerations are secondary in this mode of analysis; for in discussions of the procession from the bourgeois to the proletarian revolution we are not dealing with sociology hut with eschatology.

zh: 因此，无论是资产阶级革命还是无产阶级革命，都不是在经验上令人信服、甚至不是有用的范畴。事实上，还可以更进一步说：社会阶级从来不曾统治，统治的是国家和政府。政治不能被还原为某种社会或经济基础，国家也不只是统治阶级的代理人。用当前社会学术语来说，政治是一个“自变量”，有其自身的逻辑和规律。政治领域当然与社会领域和经济领域相互作用，任何既定政治安排中某些群体获得的利益也远多于其他群体；但政治权力的行使也有其自身的动力。因此，试图围绕所谓从一个统治阶级到另一个统治阶级的演进组织历史是徒劳的；然而这种演进恰恰是红色十月之争所预设的。于是，那一事件再一次被证明嵌入在一个比俄国历史的事实本身更宏大的形而上学之中。
en: Neither the bourgeois revolution nor the proletarian revolution, then, is an empirically compelling, or even a useful, category. Indeed, it is possible to go still further and say that social classes never rule: state and governments do. Politics cannot be reduced to some social or economic base, and the state is not simply the agent of a ruling class. Politics is an “independent variable,” as current sociological terminology has it, with its own logic and laws. The political sphere, of course, interacts with the social and the economic spheres, and some groups profit far more than others from any given political arrangement; but the exercise of political power also has a dynamic of its own. It is thus futile to try to organize history around the putative progression from one dominant class to another; yet such a progression is precisely what the debate over Red October presupposes. And so once again, that event turns out to be embedded in a metaphysic vaster than the brute events of Russian history.

zh: 因为无产阶级十月的神话，就是被异化、被非人化的群众战胜一切苦难和剥夺的神话。在这种末世论视角中，苦难是真正人性的标准，对马克思如此，对陀思妥耶夫斯基也如此。既然剧烈的危机使苦难最为尖锐，那么战争和1917年的社会崩溃就赋予了俄国生活中受侮辱与受损害者以最典型的人性地位。因为1917年的苦难不是神话，而是最残酷的经验事实。在这种情况下，弱小的俄国无产阶级确实可以在其自封的领袖眼中，并在全世界许多社会主义者眼中，显得是普遍阶级，是历史逻辑的承担者。于是，赤裸的神话变成了一股强大的经验力量，成为整个荒诞的苏维埃冒险不可或缺的发射台。
en: For the myth of proletarian October is the myth of the triumph of the alienated and dehumanized masses over all their sufferings and deprivations. In this eschatological perspective, suffering is the criterion of authentic humanity, for Marx no less than for Dostoevsky. And since intense crisis makes suffering most acute, the war and the social collapse of 1917 conferred on the humiliated and offended of Russian life quintessential human status. For the suffering of 1917 was no myth, but the most cruel empirical fact. In these circumstances, the modest Russian proletariat could indeed appear in the eyes of its self-appointed leaders, and in those of many socialists throughout the world, to be the universal class and the bearer of the logic of history. Thus patent myth became a mighty empirical force, the indispensable launching pad of the whole fantastic Soviet adventure.
